verdict: NEEDS_REREAD: coverage is real and mostly accurate (all 30 files in DroppyCode/Services/Providers are assigned, line counts match `wc -l` exactly), but R041 misstates the Claude handshake argv, R044 omits two whole algorithms (the Copilot model filter and the entire account.getQuota percent/skip logic), and several load-bearing details (persisted-seed identity, dead per-turn state, fallback auth branches) are missing across R039/R043/R046.
gaps: R041 / ClaudeSession.swift:185-193 - the handshake argv is described as "the argv omits --include-partial-messages and adds --no-session-persistence". It is not a delta of the session argv: it is a fixed, much shorter list `-p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --no-session-persistence --setting-sources user,project,local`, with no --permission-prompt-tool, no --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions, no --permission-mode, no --mcp-config, no --append-system-prompt. A port following the report's wording would launch the catalog probe with the full session argv.

R041 / ClaudeSession.swift:201-204 - handshake() requires `response.commands` to be a non-nil array before it will return anything; if the CLI answers the initialize without a `commands` array it throws "Claude could not load its commands." even though the caller (ProviderRegistry.loadClaudeCatalog, ProviderRegistry.swift:498-502) only wants `.models`. The report records the two error strings but never states that a missing `commands` key kills the Claude model catalog too.

R044 / CopilotSession.swift:407 - listModels skips every entry where `model["policy"]["state"] == "disabled"`. The report lists `.policy.state` among the fields read and documents the "unconfigured" detail string, but never mentions the disabled filter, so a port would surface models the CLI will refuse.

R044 / CopilotSession.swift:444-467 - readPlanLimits has no entry at all in feature_notes. Missing: a snapshot is skipped when `isUnlimitedEntitlement == true` or when `entitlementRequests` is absent or <= 0; percent is `max(0, min(100, 100 - remainingPercentage))` when remainingPercentage exists, otherwise `min(100, usedRequests / entitlementRequests * 100)`; `resetDate` is parsed with a plain ISO8601DateFormatter and then retried with `formatOptions = [.withFullDate]` (CopilotSession.swift:470-475); the whole read returns nil when no window survives; and the plan name is a SECOND request (account.getCurrentAuth) whose `authInfo.copilotUser.copilot_plan` is wrapped as "Copilot <plan>".

R044 / CopilotSession.swift:428-439 - authStatus's non-happy paths are undocumented: a failed connect() returns .unknown, a failed account.getCurrentAuth request returns .unknown, and a null or missing `authInfo` returns .signedOut. Only the " · no Copilot access" suffix made it into the report.

R046 / ProviderRegistry.swift:780 - the opencode auth branch's fallback is stated only as far as the credential parse. When no U+25CF line is found the result is `result.succeeded ? .signedOut : .unknown`, not an unconditional .signedOut. A port that hardcodes .signedOut will show "Not signed in" for a CLI that merely failed to run.

R043 / CommandCodeAPI.swift:349-359 - the report gives the nine seed detail strings but never the seed ids or names. Those exact ids are load-bearing twice over: they are what goes into the persisted "providerModelCatalogs" blob, and ProviderRegistry.loadCatalog compares `models(for: .commandcode) == Self.commandcodeSeed` (ProviderRegistry.swift:464) to decide whether to re-probe. The ids are claude-sonnet-5 (isDefault), claude-fable-5-1, claude-opus-5, gpt-6-astra, gpt-5.6-sol, google/gemini-3.8-flash, deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash, moonshotai/kimi-k3, zai-org/glm-5.3, with names "Claude Sonnet 5", "Claude Fable 5.1", "Claude Opus 5", "GPT-6 Astra", "GPT-5.6 Sol", "Gemini 3.8 Flash", "DeepSeek V4 Flash", "Kimi K3", "GLM 5.3".

R039 / AntigravitySession.swift:23-24, 88, 150-151 - the report says runtimeMode and interactionMode are "refreshed on each send". They are written on every send and then never read: modeArguments is called once at line 88 with `configuration.runtimeMode` / `configuration.interactionMode`, so the two stored properties are dead after init. The practical consequence for the port (a mid-thread runtime-mode or plan/build switch cannot reach `agy` without relaunching the process) is not stated anywhere. Contrast PiSession.swift:279-288, where the same switch does take effect because it is rewritten into the gate file every turn.

R039 / ACPSession.swift:381-385 - applyConfigOptions sets `effortConfigID = nil` and `fastConfigID = nil` at the top of every call. A config_option_update or a set_config_option reply that omits the thought_level or model_config entries therefore drops the effort slider and the Fast toggle for the rest of the session. The report describes what the branches build but not this reset.

R039 / ACPSession.swift:534-535 - the `config_option_update` session/update notification is handled (it re-runs applyConfigOptions, which re-emits .models with a new current model / effort scale / fast tier). It appears only as the bare word "configOptions" inside persisted_fields; there is no feature note saying the agent can push a live model or effort change mid-session. `agent_thought_chunk`, `plan` and `available_commands_update` are likewise handled but never named in feature_notes.

R040 / OpenAICompatibleSession.swift:437-446, 471-482, 808-812 - no feature note covers cancellation. interrupt() sets `interrupted`, cancels sendTask, roundTask and sseDrain, and resumes every pending approval continuation with `false` (i.e. an in-flight approval is silently treated as a decline); stop() does all that plus sets isStopping and nils sessionID, which makes isRunning false (line 240). finishInterrupted resolves approvals the same way and emits .turnCompleted(.interrupted). Also unstated: `approveAllRemaining` (set by the "always" option at line 450) is reset per turn at line 292, which is what makes the label "Approve for turn" honest.

R046 / ProviderRegistry.swift:626-641 - refreshCredits has no 25-second watchdog and no `defer` around `loadingCredits.remove(provider)` (unlike refreshPlanLimits at lines 550-566), and when the key is empty it clears `credits[provider]` but leaves `creditsFetchedAt[provider]` intact. The report flattens both reads into "the read runs on its own task" and states only the credits-clearing half.
contradictions: R042 (CodexSession) and R044 (CopilotSession) both file `sendsVersion:` as an unresolved question ("whether sendsVersion: false omits the jsonrpc version field or some client-version field"). It is settled one grep away in an adjacent bundle: JSONRPC.swift:109 `if sendsVersion { message["jsonrpc"] = "2.0" }`. Codex's app-server is the only connection built with `sendsVersion: false` (CodexSession.swift:508) and therefore must receive frames with NO `jsonrpc` member, while ACP (ACPSession.swift:117) and Copilot (CopilotSession.swift:494) must receive `"jsonrpc": "2.0"`. Two reports leaving this open risks the port sending a uniform envelope.

R041 asks who populates PlanLimits.Window.detail ("declared with default nil but never set anywhere in this file"); R040 answers it for Z.ai (ZaiAPI window details "<current> of <usage> credits" / "<current> of <usage> calls"). Not a factual conflict, but the two reports were not reconciled, so the family leaves a field looking unused when it is not.

R041 asks which readers call PlanLimitsReader.windowTitle(minutes:); R040 (ZaiAPI) and R045 (PiPlanLimits, "Codex · " + windowTitle(minutes: limit_window_seconds / 60)) and R042 (Codex plan windows) all name callers. Same unreconciled-question pattern.

R044's header note claims "session delete was verified live" and then admits no session.delete call exists in the file; nothing else in the family accounts for a Copilot session ever being deleted. Either the header comment is stale or the delete lives outside Services/Providers and no reader in this family chased it.
cross_cutting_findings: Three different JSON-RPC dialects ride on the same JSONRPCConnection with different envelopes and framings, and the port must keep them apart: ACP (ACPSession.swift:117, sendsVersion true, default framing), Codex app-server (CodexSession.swift:508, sendsVersion FALSE, default framing), Copilot SDK (CopilotSession.swift:494, sendsVersion true, StdioProcess framing: .contentLength). Pi and Command Code and Antigravity use line/JSONL framing instead (PiSession.swift framing: .lines).

Every unsupported inbound JSON-RPC request is answered with error code -32601, but the message differs by provider: ACPSession.swift:559 sends "Method not found"; CodexSession and CopilotSession send "Droppy Code does not support <method>." A port should not unify these.

The client identity string "droppy-code" / title "Droppy Code" / version AppInfo.version is sent on four separate handshakes with different key paths: ACP `clientInfo` in initialize, Codex `clientInfo` in initialize (CodexSession.swift:517), Copilot `clientName` in session.create/resume plus the ping payload `{"message":"droppy-code"}` (CopilotSession.swift:496), Claude control request ids prefixed "droppy-code-<n>".

RuntimeMode.rawValue and InteractionMode.rawValue are an on-disk contract, not just an in-memory enum: PiSession.swift:281-286 writes them verbatim into the per-session gate JSON, and the shipped TypeScript in PiCLI.extensionSource compares them against the literals "fullAccess", "autoAcceptEdits", "auto" and "plan". No report in this family states that those raw values must match exactly, and the enum is declared outside the bundle.

Four independent "install a helper file next to the app, only when the bytes differ" patterns exist and must all be ported: CommandCodeAPI.installMod() writing droppy-code-approvals.ts, PiCLI.installExtension() writing droppy-gate.ts, MCPBridge.installBridge(), plus the per-session scratch directories (Command Code approvals dir, Pi gates dir). All are under Application Support on macOS.

Runtime-mode changes reach the provider by three different mechanisms, and only one survives without restarting the process: a live protocol call (Claude set_permission_mode, Copilot session.permissions.setMode, Codex per-turn approvalPolicy/sandboxPolicy, ACP set_config_option), a rewritten gate file (Pi, Command Code), or launch flags only (Antigravity, ACP launchArguments, Copilot isExperimentalMode). Antigravity and the ACP launch flags need a session restart; the family never says so in one place.

Only two providers expose a cancellable, interruptible turn over the wire (Claude control `interrupt`, Codex `turn/interrupt`, Copilot `session.abort`, ACP `session/cancel`, Pi `abort`). Antigravity and Command Code have no interrupt message at all and rely on SIGTERM plus an isStopping/interruptRequested flag to keep the UI from reporting a crash (AntigravitySession.swift:165-175, CommandCodeSession.swift:229-236). A Windows port has no SIGTERM equivalent with those semantics and must decide what replaces it.

Three providers pass MCP configuration by three different channels that all originate in the same settings: --mcp-config + --strict-mcp-config (Claude), config.mcp_servers inside thread params (Codex), --allowed-mcp-server-names <ids...> (Antigravity), MCPSessionOverrides.copilotArguments() (Copilot), MCPSessionOverrides.opencodeEnvironment() merged into the child env (opencode), GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH (antigravity), and DROPPY_CODE_MCP_BRIDGE / DROPPY_CODE_MCP_CONFIG env vars read by the Pi and Command Code helper scripts.

Two UserDefaults keys and one alternate defaults suite carry the whole provider cache: "providerModelCatalogs" and "providerModelCatalogDates" on UserDefaults.standard, "recentSlashCommands" on (CaptureRun.defaults ?? .standard) (ProviderRegistry.swift:47-49, 158, 697). The catalogs blob is rewritten whole on every change, and at load time every cached row is re-sorted through ACPSession.orderedEfforts (ProviderRegistry.swift:167-172) - a migration step that only exists as that one map call.
thin_reports: R044 (CopilotSession.swift, 1075 lines) - dense and accurate on the event stream and permission model, but the static half of the file is compressed almost to nothing: listModels, authStatus and readPlanLimits (CopilotSession.swift:400-475) get field lists in persisted_fields and title strings in ui_elements, with no feature note describing their actual logic. The disabled-model filter and the entire quota percent/skip computation are absent. Needs a targeted re-read of lines 400-475.

verdict: NEEDS_REREAD - the three reports are mostly accurate and unusually specific, but R037 states a provider-config rule that the source contradicts, R038 states the wrong field-value fallback chain for MCPStore, and the OAuth callback page's verbatim assets plus several protocol field names, unreachable branches and dead APIs are missing.
contradictions: R037 vs source, MCPProviderConfig.swift:129-133: R037's feature_notes say "Claude, Codex and Gemini omit an empty env or headers object entirely". False for Gemini remote servers - `gemini(_:)` emits `"headers": .object(server.headers.mapValues(JSONValue.string))` unconditionally, exactly like Copilot (:60). Only the Gemini LOCAL branch guards `env` with `if !server.env.isEmpty` (:139). R037 also contradicts itself: its persisted_fields line for Gemini says `remote {httpUrl, headers}` with no optionality marker while the feature note says it is omitted. A port following the feature note writes a different gemini-settings.json than Droppy does.

R038 vs source, MCPStore.swift:64-70: R038 describes `value(for:of:)` as "draft first, else the Keychain secret for a .secret field, else the connection's stored value, else field.defaultValue". The source is an if/else-if: a `.secret` field reads ONLY the Keychain and never falls through to `connections[id]?.values[key]`; a non-secret field never reads the Keychain. Both kinds then fall to `field.defaultValue ?? ""`. The reported chain would make a port show a stale plaintext value for a secret field whose Keychain item is missing (including every CaptureRun, where MCPKeychain.value returns nil by design, MCPKeychain.swift:12).

R037 internal: its MCPProbe entry leaves "whether the 240-second mcp-remote deadline is ever reached in practice" unresolved, while its own MCPProviderConfig entry records that `mcp-remote` is minted only by `acpServers(allowsHTTP: false)` (MCPProviderConfig.swift:99). Those two facts together settle it - see the unreachable-branch gap below - but the report files them as an open question instead.
cross_cutting_findings: Path literals the three reports all deferred are resolvable and matter: `AppInfo.name` is `Bundle.main.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: "CFBundleDisplayName") as? String ?? "Droppy Code"` (Core/Support/Text.swift:4) and `Storage.root` is `~/Library/Application Support/<AppInfo.name>`, overridable by `CaptureRun.storageRoot` (Services/Store/Storage.swift:19-25). So mcp.json and custom-mcp.json sit directly in that folder and MCPPaths.directory is `<that>/mcp`.

Directory-case collision nobody flagged: `MCPBridge.installBridge()` writes to `<Application Support>/<AppInfo.name>/MCP/droppy-mcp-bridge.mjs` (MCPBridgeSource.swift:243-246, capital MCP, built from `FileManager.urls(for:.applicationSupportDirectory)` and NOT from Storage.root), while `MCPPaths.directory` is `Storage.root/mcp` (MCP.swift:231, lowercase). On a default case-insensitive macOS volume and on Windows these are the same folder, so the bridge .mjs lands beside claude.json / codex.json / copilot.json / gemini-settings.json / proxy-port / managed.json; on a case-sensitive volume they are two folders. A second consequence: under CaptureRun, MCPPaths moves with Storage.root but the bridge directory does not.

Complete file inventory under MCPPaths.directory, which no single report gives: claude.json, codex.json, copilot.json (MCP.swift:236-241), gemini-settings.json (MCPProviderConfig.swift:238), proxy-port (MCPProxy.swift:15), managed.json (MCPExternalSync.swift:52). `writeAll([])` deletes only the first four (MCPProviderConfig.swift:150-152); proxy-port is never deleted by anything, so a reinstall reuses the old port, and managed.json is deleted exactly once by the migration (MCPExternalSync.swift:27).

The consumer side of every generated artifact is unrecorded, so the port has the file formats but not the invocations: ClaudeSession.swift:96 passes `--mcp-config <path> --strict-mcp-config` (both flags, only when claudeConfigPath() is non-nil); AntigravitySession.swift:83-84 passes `--allowed-mcp-server-names` followed by connectedIDs(); ProviderRegistry.swift:274 sets `GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH` to gemini-settings.json (the Gemini file is consumed by the Antigravity provider, not a "Gemini" provider); ProviderRegistry.swift:272 merges opencodeEnvironment() for `.opencode`; CopilotSession.swift:486 appends copilotArguments(); CodexSession.swift:257-261 merges codexOverrides() into `params["config"]["mcp_servers"]`; ACPSession.swift:254 passes acpServers(allowsHTTP: supportsHTTPMCP) as the `mcpServers` field of session/new and session/load.

The env var that carries the bridge path is never named in any report: PiSession.swift:105-110 and CommandCodeSession.swift:174-179 set `DROPPY_CODE_MCP_BRIDGE` to the installed .mjs path, and set `DROPPY_CODE_MCP_CONFIG` to MCPPaths.claudeConfigURL.path only when that file exists. R037 names DROPPY_CODE_MCP_CONFIG but not DROPPY_CODE_MCP_BRIDGE.

MCPHub's only consumer is OpenAICompatibleSession.swift:510 (tools()), :898 (parse) and :904 (call) - the in-app model-API provider. R037 left that unresolved. MCPHub.terminateAll() is called from AppDelegate.swift:54.

Token expiry spans R037 and R038 and is mis-stated as unconditional: `storeSession` writes `expires_at` only when the token response carried `expires_in` (MCPOAuth.swift:698-700), and `accessToken` treats a missing `expires_at` as never-expiring (`guard let expiresAt = ... else { return false }`, MCPOAuth.swift:172). Combined with MCPProxy.swift:355-361, the proxy's "401 -> fetch token again and replay once" does NOT force a refresh; it calls the same `accessToken` and, absent an expiry, gets the identical cached token, so the replay is a byte-identical retry. Neither report states this.

Custom-server migration risk spans R032 and R038: `MCPCustomServer.Variable` uses the synthesized decoder with no default for `isSecret` (MCPCustom.swift:15-19), so a stored variable object missing that key throws; because the throw happens inside `decodeIfPresent([Variable]...)` (MCPCustom.swift:46,48) and `MCPStore.load()` decodes the whole array with `try?` (MCPStore.swift:245-248), one bad variable silently drops EVERY custom server, not one. R032 raised the decoder question; nobody carried it to the blast radius.
gaps: MCPCatalog.swift - no report records each field's `kind`, which decides whether a value goes to mcp.json or the Keychain. Exactly three built-in fields are non-secret: gitlab `instance` (.text, :31), filesystem `root` (.path, :83), sqlite `path` (.path, :389). Every other declared field is `.secret`, including postgres `url` (:372) and mongodb `url` (:407) whose values are full connection strings. So those three keys are the only ones that ever appear in `MCPConnection.values` in mcp.json for a built-in server. R032's persisted_fields lumps all field keys as "mcp.json values or Keychain entries".

MCPOAuth.swift:903 - the callback page's inline logo is a single `<path d="...">` of roughly 1.4 KB of exact coordinates. R037 paraphrases it ("a sprout/leaf mark plus two round dots (circle near 63,43 radius 5 ...)"). A parity port cannot reconstruct the mark from that; the `d` string must be captured verbatim, along with `<!DOCTYPE html>`, `<html lang="en">`, `<meta charset="utf-8">`, `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`, `* { box-sizing: border-box; }` and `html, body { margin: 0; padding: 0; }`, none of which R037 lists.

MCPOAuth.swift:19-44 - the error-message composition rule is missing. R037 prints a flat list of strings, but `discoveryFailed`, `metadataFailed`, `registrationFailed` and `tokenFailed` render as `<base> <detail>` when the detail is non-empty and `<base>` alone when empty, while `callbackFailed` and `network` render the DETAIL ALONE when non-empty and their base only when empty. So the user-visible text for a 404 during metadata lookup is "The server's sign-in details didn't make sense. The server answered 404.", not either string on its own.

MCPOAuth.swift:209-211, 225-232 - protected-resource metadata field names are only half recorded. R037 names `authorization_servers` and `resource` but not `scopes_supported` (the array whose non-empty strings become resourceScopes, which then drive both the registration `scope` and the authorization-URL `scope`), and it does not state that only the FIRST element of `authorization_servers` is used.

MCPProbe.swift:196-197 and :277-278 - the probe reads the server name and version from `result.serverInfo.name` and `result.serverInfo.version`. R037 says the probe "returns the server name, version" without ever naming the `serverInfo` object, so a port has no field path for the value it persists as `MCPConnection.serverVersion`.

MCPHub.swift:281 and MCPProbe.swift:89 - `checkReply` falls back to the literal string "unknown error" when a JSON-RPC error object has no `message`. That string reaches the user through LocalizedError (MCPHubError.server / MCPProbeError.malformed, which renders "The server sent something unexpected: unknown error"). Neither report lists it among the UI strings.

MCPProbe.swift:308 - `postJSON` builds `URLRequest(url:timeoutInterval: 30)` for every remote probe request. R037's MCPProbe timeout notes cover only the 240/90 second stdio deadlines and the 5 ms poll; the 30-second per-request HTTP timeout is absent, and it differs from MCPHub, which passes the per-call timeout (60/120/30) into its URLRequest (MCPHub.swift:453).

MCPProxy.swift:17-24 + MCP.swift:165 - the proxy-port file is written as a side effect of the FIRST read of `MCPProxy.port`, and that first read happens inside `MCPCatalogEntry.resolve` via `MCPProxy.url(for: id)`, i.e. potentially before `start()` is ever called. R038 records the file's format but presents it as proxy-lifecycle state rather than as something a pure-looking `resolve()` triggers.

MCPProxy.swift:118-128 + MCPStore.swift:22-27 - the repick path leaves the provider configs stale. `MCPStore.init` calls `MCPProxy.shared.start()` and then `exportAll()`, which bakes `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp/<id>` into claude.json, codex.json, copilot.json and gemini-settings.json. If the listener afterwards enters `.failed`, `repickPort()` moves the port and rewrites proxy-port, but nothing re-runs `MCPProviderConfig.writeAll`, so every config written this launch points at the dead port. Neither R038's proxy entry nor its store entry connects these.

MCPBridgeSource.swift:49-56, :74-151, :225-237 - the bridge never kills a spawned child. `withTimeout` rejects after CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000 and `loadMCPTools` catches and skips the server, but there is no `child.kill()`, `unref()` or SIGTERM anywhere in the file (grep confirms zero hits), so a server that hangs during initialize or tools/list leaves a live process for the lifetime of the Pi / Command Code host. This is the opposite of MCPHub, which tracks every child in `liveProcesses` and SIGKILLs it at quit. R037 describes the timeout as a plain skip.

MCPBridgeSource.swift:154 - the bridge's `postMessage` sets only Content-Type and Accept (plus lowercase `mcp-session-id`). It does NOT send `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-06-18`, which both MCPHub (:462) and MCPProbe (:314) do send. R037 lists the bridge's headers correctly but does not flag the divergence, which a port would silently normalize away.

MCPProxy.swift:308 and :369-378 - the proxy forwards the client's HTTP method verbatim, so GET (the streamable-HTTP SSE channel) and DELETE (session teardown) pass through unchanged; no report states which methods are supported. It also copies back only Content-Type, Mcp-Session-Id and Cache-Control, so `WWW-Authenticate` on a 401 is dropped - any client that tried OAuth discovery through a proxy route would see a bare 401.

MCPProxy.swift:263-275 - `readBody` on an early EOF (`isComplete || error != nil`) forwards whatever bytes arrived, so a request truncated below its declared Content-Length is relayed upstream rather than refused. R038 documents the 413/411/400 refusals but not this silent-truncation path.

MCPHub.swift:59 vs :76-95 - the `failed` set is consulted only by `tools()`; `call()` never checks it, so a server whose `listTools` threw is still launched again on a direct tool call. Separately, the `didRestart`/`dead` one-restart policy lives entirely in `ensureStdio` (:307-319): the HTTP path (:419-450) has no restart or dead state at all, and `initialized` is only cleared by `stop()`. R037 presents the restart policy without scoping it to stdio.

MCPStore.swift:335 - on probe success, `connectedAt`, `serverVersion` and `tools` are written only `if var connection = connections[entry.id]` exists, while `states[entry.id] = .connected(toolCount:)` is set unconditionally. A probe that succeeds with no connection row therefore shows as connected but is filtered out of `enabledServers` (which requires `connectedAt != nil`, :42) and so reaches no provider config. R038 states the success path without the guard.

MCPKeychain.swift:37-49 - `set()` calls `SecItemUpdate` with a query that carries no `kSecAttrAccessible`; only the `SecItemAdd` fallback (:47) applies `kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked`. An item created by an earlier build keeps whatever accessibility it had forever. R037 records the add attribute but not that updates never migrate it - a persisted attribute whose migration behavior is unstated.

Unreachable / dead code nobody classified, which the contract explicitly asks for: (a) `MCPProxy.stop()` (MCPProxy.swift:142) has no call site anywhere in the repository - the proxy is never shut down; R038 raised it as a question rather than resolving it. (b) `MCPOAuth.refreshIfNeeded(serverID:)` (MCPOAuth.swift:193) has no call site anywhere; R037 documents it as shipped behavior. (c) `MCPProxy.Route.headers` is always `[:]` at both registration sites (MCPStore.swift:284 and :310), so route-configured headers are dead configuration. (d) MCPProbe's `isOAuth` branch - the 240-second deadline (MCPProbe.swift:115) and the stderr "Unauthorized"/"invalid_grant" -> unauthorizedOAuth mapping (:217-219) - is unreachable for every built-in server: the only producer of a `mcp-remote` argument is `MCPProviderConfig.acpServers(allowsHTTP: false)` (:99), whose output goes to ACPSession.swift:254 and never to the probe, and the probe's sole caller (MCPStore.swift:313) always passes `entry.resolve(values:)`. Only a user-authored custom stdio server whose args literally contain "mcp-remote" can reach it.

MCPOAuth.swift:404-406 - the sign-in callback listener sets only `requiredLocalEndpoint = .hostPort(host: "127.0.0.1", port: .any)` and, unlike MCPProxy (:97), does not set `requiredInterfaceType = .loopback`. R037 records the endpoint but not the missing interface restriction, which is the kind of detail a port's socket-binding code has to decide.
thin_reports: R037 - not thin overall (MCPHub, MCPProbe, MCPProviderConfig and MCPBridgeSource are dense and mostly correct), but its MCPOAuth.swift entry is thin for a 929-line file: it paraphrases the verbatim callback-page SVG instead of capturing it, omits the base+detail error-message composition rule, omits `scopes_supported`, omits that `expires_at` is optional and that a session without it never refreshes, and omits that the callback listener does not restrict its interface type. That one file deserves a re-read.

verdict: NEEDS_REREAD — R031 must re-read Hydra.swift for the prompt corpus verbatim and R014 must re-classify HydraRunMetricsView; R005 has one inverted tie-break rule and several undescribed behaviors in AppModel+Hydra.swift.
contradictions: R031 (Hydra.swift, state_owned) says "HydraPrompts.verificationMarkers (28 markers)" while its own feature_notes says "verificationMarkers (34 exact substrings...)" and lists 34. The source has exactly 34 entries (DroppyCode/Core/Models/Hydra.swift:1128-1137). The state_owned count is wrong.

R005 (AppModel+Hydra.swift, feature_notes) says "The head cap is [pair?.maxHeads, settings.hydraMaxHeads].compactMap{$0}.min(); with neither, heads run uncapped." R031 (Hydra.swift) says the opposite for the runtime effect: HydraLaunch.hasRoom uses `maxHeads ?? uncappedConcurrency` with uncappedConcurrency = 8 (Hydra.swift:168-173). A port following R005 alone would let unbounded heads run, which the source comment explicitly guards against (21 simultaneous heads forcing a force quit).

R005 (HydraCookbook+Resolve.swift) says model(named:) ties are "broken by the later position in registry.models(for:)". The source breaks ties toward the EARLIER position: `matches.max { ... return options.firstIndex(lhs)! > options.firstIndex(rhs)! }` makes the higher-index element compare as smaller, so max() returns the lowest-index option (DroppyCode/App/HydraCookbook+Resolve.swift:52-61). R005 has the direction inverted.

R031 (Hydra.swift, feature_notes) says copilotAgents "deliberately passes no tools list for the scout", implying the worker does get one, and its persisted_fields lists "tools" among the emitted Copilot customAgents keys. AppSettings defaults for this family are stated nowhere in the four reports (DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:743-760): hydraEnabled default TRUE, hydraDefaultEnabled TRUE, hasSeenHydraIntro FALSE, hydraIsolateHeads TRUE, hydraTempersHeadEffort TRUE, hydraAutoMerge FALSE, hydraReviewHeads FALSE, hydraAutoClearFinished FALSE, hydraShowsHeadDetails FALSE, hydraMaxHeads has NO default and is passed through HydraPair.clampedCap on load (1...8). DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/HydraButton.swift:212-226: the right-click items carry checkmark state (`isChecked: isOn` / `isChecked: !isOn`) and the "Turn Hydra on" item in the Hydra-off-in-Settings branch writes `settings.hydraEnabled = true` AND calls `setHydra(true, ...)`. cross_cutting_findings: Hydra is ON by default on a fresh install (AppSettings.swift:743, hydraEnabled default true) and new chats inherit hydraEnabled = true from UserDefaults key "hydraDefaultEnabled" (Library.swift:195-201). The Windows port must ship the same defaults or the whole feature silently changes state.

Every Hydra persisted type decodes tolerantly through `container.value(_:default:)` (Coding.swift) with deliberate defaults, most importantly HydraHeadInfo.status defaulting to .stopped and never .completed (Hydra.swift:404-406) and HydraPair.maxHeads clamped to 1...8 on decode (Hydra.swift:90). The port's schema needs the same per-field fallbacks rather than a strict decoder.

Concurrency ceiling: with no pair cap and no Hydra-page cap, eight heads run at once (HydraLaunch.uncappedConcurrency = 8, Hydra.swift:168) and the rest wait. This is a hard product constraint, not an implementation detail.

Scratch/path handling is heavily POSIX: isScratchPath (AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:158-173) keys on /tmp, /private/tmp, /var/folders, /private/var/folders, ~/Library and dot-directories directly under home, and relies on NSString.standardizingPath dropping a leading /private only while the file exists. hydraProject (AppModel+Hydra.swift:281-299) requires `expanded.hasPrefix("/")` and walks upward terminating at "/". Neither has a Windows equivalent and no report proposed one.

Worktree copy folder naming is the sweeper's contract: "<longest project slug>-<persona slug>[-<round>]-<8 lowercase hex of thread UUID>" (AppModel+Hydra.swift:494-497 and the orphan matcher at :1040-1053). Change the naming on Windows and the orphan sweep either deletes nothing or deletes the wrong folder.

Three separate code paths parse the SAME lead-authored strings, so the writers and readers must stay byte-identical in the port: Hydra.swift reportMessage/landingLine -> HydraReportsPopover.parse; AppModel+HydraMerge merge note -> HydraMergePopover.parse (files line regex requires U+2212 MINUS and backticked target/branch); HydraPrompts fallbackPolicy fence -> HydraDelegationStream/delegations. A paraphrased prompt or an ASCII hyphen breaks the UI silently.

The fence dialects diverge on purpose and the port must keep both: Hydra.swift delegationOpener accepts ```hydra, ```hydra-sent and ```hydra-leaving (Hydra.swift:996-998), while the streaming reader and the hand-written state machine accept only ```hydra and ```hydra-sent (HydraDelegationStream.swift:17 and the 16-state readOpener).

Native-provider wiring is three different shapes from one HydraLaunch: Claude `--agents` JSON (keys description/prompt/background/tools/model/effort, model skipped when == "default"), Copilot customAgents (name/displayName/description/prompt/infer/model/reasoningEffort, model skipped when == "auto", tools NEVER emitted), Codex config overrides (agents.max_concurrent_threads_per_session, agents.default_subagent_model, agents.default_subagent_reasoning_effort, features.multi_agent always true, features.multi_agent_v2.expose_spawn_agent_model_overrides only with routable profiles). Hydra.swift:742-846.

GitLab merge requests do not go through the shared forge layer: `glab mr create --title <t> --description <b> --yes [--repo <web url, user/password stripped>] --source-branch <s> --target-branch <t>` with a 300 s timeout, preceded by `glab auth status` (30 s), one auth retry and one `--recover` retry (AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:329-377). The Windows port needs the same flag set and the same two retry conditions.

The auto-merge never checks out a branch: it write-trees the team's paths, commits with commitWork(tree, parent: head), and moves the ref with updateRef(expecting: ownBranch ? nil : head) after re-reading commitHash (AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:213-243). Any port that uses `git checkout`/`git commit` here changes user-visible behavior.
thin_reports: R014 — for DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/HydraRunMetricsView.swift (398 lines) the report documents metrics, phase math and card layout in detail but never establishes reachability; a one-line repo grep shows zero call sites, so the file is dead code and the report presents it as shipped UI. The port contract explicitly requires classifying unreachable code with evidence. The report also leaves "where it is instantiated" as an unresolved question that the reference checkout answers definitively.

R031 — for DroppyCode/Core/Models/Hydra.swift (1345 lines) the majority of the file by volume is exact prompt text (policy(for:), howToWork, howToReport, briefRule, verificationRule, projectRule, autoMergeRule, reviewRule, reportStyleRule, workerPrompt, scoutPrompt, fallbackPolicy body). The report captures a handful of fragments and otherwise paraphrases, while the port contract requires these verbatim. It also miscounts verificationMarkers (28 vs 34) and misstates the Copilot `tools` emission, both of which are simple transcription errors indicating the tail of the file was summarized rather than transcribed.

R005 — for DroppyCode/App/AppModel+Hydra.swift (1082 lines) the landing/merge/watchdog machinery is genuinely well covered and verified accurate, but three shipped behaviors in the first 400 lines are absent entirely (setHydra adopting the remembered pair's lead model and effort, the keepsModel discard of worker model/effort on provider fallback, and the whole head-profile routing precedence in insertHydraHead). The HydraCookbook+Resolve.swift section (69 lines) also inverts the catalogue tie-break direction, which suggests the comparator was read but not evaluated.

verdict: NEEDS_REREAD - six of seven reports hold up well against the source, but R008 (ThreadRuntime.swift, 3637 lines) never describes the ProviderEvent dispatch case by case and states a session-ID rule that the API-key branch contradicts, so the protocol and session-lifecycle spec for the port is wrong as written.
gaps: ThreadRuntime.swift:2079-2195 - the ProviderEvent switch, the single most protocol-critical control flow in this family, is not described case by case anywhere in R008. Unreported handled events: `.title` (2154-2158) is accepted ONLY when `turns.count <= 1 && !thread.hasCustomTitle && app.textEngine(preferring: thread.provider) == nil`, and the accepted title is run through `TextCleanup.withoutEmDashes`; `.modeChanged` (2146-2147) writes `thread.interactionMode` from the provider; `.commands` (2150-2153) stores the command list keyed by `thread.worktreePath ?? project.path`; `.usage` (2132-2139) bumps `saveRevision` AND calls `providers.invalidateCredits(provider)` + `providers.invalidatePlanLimits(provider)`; `.models` (2148-2149) calls `updateCatalog`; `.diff` (2140-2141) and `.assistantMessageID` (2159-2160) record only while `currentTurnID != nil`; `.requestResolved` (2129-2131) clears the id from BOTH approvals and questions; `.toolStarted` (2098-2101) starts `watchCommand` only for `call.kind == .command`; `.toolUpdated` (2104-2113) both settles the command snapshot when a command tool leaves `.running` and routes a finished tool to `hydraToolFinished` via `hydraToolHeads[id]`.

ThreadRuntime.swift:1430-1491 vs 1497-1567 - the API-key and CLI session-start paths differ in three ways a port will get wrong, none reported. (a) `isStartingSession = true` is set only in the CLI branch (1534); an API session that exits during `start()` is therefore NOT protected by the `if isStartingSession { break }` guard in the `.exited` handler (2172). (b) The API branch writes `providerSessionID` directly (1490) instead of going through `recordSessionID` (1567, 1570-1577), so the `unsentSessionID` hold-back does not exist for DeepSeek/Meta/Z.ai. (c) The API retry predicate is inline `thread.providerSessionID != nil && thread.providerResumeAt == nil && allowNewSession && session === candidate && !Task.isCancelled` (1479), not `Self.startsOver(after:resuming:)` (1546); it emits no "no longer has this conversation" notice and never clears `providerResumeAt`, unlike the CLI branch (1546-1553).

ThreadRuntime.swift:1453-1458 - the API-key session factory switch has an unreachable `default: DeepSeekSession(configuration: configuration)` arm (the branch is already gated on `thread.provider.isAPIKeyBased`, which Provider.swift restricts to .deepseek/.meta/.zai). R008 classifies no code in this file as unreachable, so a port cannot tell whether this arm is meaningful.

ThreadRuntime.swift:1140-1153 - `handleLocalCommand` also calls `app.providers.recordCommand("plan", for:)` / `recordCommand("compact", for:)`, which feeds the `recent` recency ranking that `SlashCommand.suggestions(_:matching:recent:)` (Provider.swift) sorts by. R008 reports the two local commands but not this side effect, and R030 documents the `recent` parameter without naming who populates it.

ThreadRuntime.swift:1655-1669 - `interrupt()` has a distinct `.starting` fast path: it clears `currentTurnID` and finishes the turn as `.interrupted` without ever calling `session.interrupt()` and without arming the 8 second watchdog, so the message that was on its way is dropped rather than sent. R008 reports only the watchdog.

ThreadRuntime.swift:1685-1695 - `resolve(_:option:)` is not just a passthrough: for a `.plan` approval with a `toolItemID` it mutates the stored `ProposedPlan.state` to `.accepted` when `option.role == .approve` and `.dismissed` otherwise, bumps `saveRevision` and schedules a save, before calling `session.resolveApproval`. Unreported by R008.

ThreadRuntime.swift:1158-1167 - `startTurn` silently converts a send into a queued follow-up in three cases: `phase != .idle`, `isReverting`, or `thread.isArchived`. R008 reports the follow-up queue but not these three implicit enqueues.

ThreadRuntime.swift:1380-1392 - `warmSession()` clears `warmup` only on success or on the phase re-check; a throwing `ensureSession` leaves `warmup` non-nil forever, permanently disabling warm starts for that runtime for the rest of the process (the comment says this is deliberate: "A start that fails is not retried on every keystroke"). Unreported.

AppModel.swift:1070-1077 - `discardThreadState` teardown ordering is unreported by R003: cancel the idle-stop task, `cancelPersistence()` BEFORE `stopSession()`, drop the runtime, `terminals.closeAll(for:)`, then optionally `Storage.deleteDocument`. The cancelPersistence-before-stopSession order is the opposite of `releaseIdleRuntime`'s `saveNow()` then `cancelPersistence()`, so a port that picks one order loses unsaved state in one of the two paths.

AutoContinue's user-facing controls are named nowhere in this family. They live in DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/LimitResumeBadge.swift:23-38: two plain buttons labelled exactly "Cancel" (help "Stop the automatic continue") and "New thread" (help "Stop the automatic continue and pick the work up in a new thread, where you can choose another model"), shown only while `model.autoContinue.resumesAt[threadID] != nil`. The post-wait wording R007 defers to the doc comment is also there, verbatim: "Usage limit reached. Auto-continue cancelled.", "Usage limit reached. Continuing in a new thread.", "Usage limit reached. Continued automatically." (lines 56-58).

AutoContinue waits are never cancelled or re-armed at teardown, and R007 left this as an open question. Grepping every `autoContinue.` call site (AppModel.swift:498, 1194; ThreadRuntime.swift:2145; LimitResumeBadge.swift:14, 23, 31, 54) confirms it: `resumesAt` and `outcomes` are in-memory only, so after a relaunch the persisted `.info` notice still reads "Usage limit reached. Continuing automatically at <time>." with no countdown, no buttons (waiting == false) and no resume. That stranded-state behavior is a shipped consequence the port must reproduce or deliberately change.

Shell.swift:331-335 - R033 says "Excluded environment keys (13)" but `excludedKeys` holds 15 entries (the list it then prints is correct). Shell.swift:144-151 - R033 says "Reader tool allowlist (51 entries)" but `readers` holds 52 (again the printed list is correct). A port sizing a table from the stated count would be wrong twice.

Text.swift:81 (`SimpleDiff.diffLimit = 200_000`) and ThreadRuntime.swift:3366 (`editDiffLimit = 200_000`) are two independent constants with different operands: `diffLimit` bounds `old.utf8.count + new.utf8.count` (the inputs) at Text.swift:101, while `editDiffLimit` bounds `diff.utf8.count` (the produced hunk) at ThreadRuntime.swift:3373 and 3397. R033 asserts "the same cap bounds command diffs in ThreadRuntime.fileEdits", conflating them.

AppSettings.swift:709 - `chatZoom` default is recorded by R003 only as "ChatZoom.defaultIndex", leaving the shipped default undocumented. It resolves to UI/Common/ChatZoom.swift:10,13: `percentages = [80, 90, 95, 100, 110, 125, 135]`, `defaultIndex = 3`, i.e. 100%, and `clamped` is `min(stepCount - 1, max(0, index))`.

Verbatim it is `anchor apple generic and certificate 1[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.2.6] and certificate leaf[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.13] and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = "NARHG44L48" and identifier "<bundleID>"`; the `leaf[subject.OU]` clause is the one that actually pins the team and is absent from the report.

It is macOS `NSHapticFeedbackManager` (trackpad-only) and has no Windows equivalent, so it belongs on the macOS-dependency list beside hdiutil/ditto/spctl/SecStaticCode.
