cross_cutting_findings: Cmd+1 through Cmd+9 are hardcoded in two places that must stay in sync: AppCommands.swift:85-88 builds nine "Thread N" buttons with `.keyboardShortcut(KeyEquivalent(Character(String(number))), modifiers: .command)` outside the ShortcutStore system, and Shortcuts.swift:255 reserves exactly those key codes (18, 19, 20, 21, 23, 22, 26, 28, 25 = digits 1-9 with .command) so no user-assignable command can take them, refused with "macOS or Droppy Code already uses this chord." R003 and R030 each describe one half; neither connects them.

Two different RuntimeMode defaults ship, and the difference is deliberate security behavior. A new thread starts on `AppSettings.defaultRuntimeMode`, which defaults to `.fullAccess` (AppSettings.swift:698), while a thread decoded from library.json whose `runtimeMode` key is missing OR type-mismatched falls back to `.supervised` (Library.swift ChatThread decoder, with the comment that a thread must never quietly come back from disk with full access). R003 and R030 each report one default; a port that uses one constant for both breaks the stated invariant.

R003's unresolved questions about ChatThread are answered inside this family by R030 and the source: `ChatThread.hydraDefaultKey = "hydraDefaultEnabled"` (Library.swift:195) - so AppSettings' `hydraDefaultEnabled` persists under that literal - and `ChatThread.untitled = "New thread"` (Library.swift:122), which is also the fallback title R008 leaves open and the string `openThreadOnLaunch` matches on.

R047's unresolved on-disk paths are answered by R033: `AppInfo.name` is CFBundleDisplayName with fallback "Droppy Code" and `AppInfo.stateDirectoryName` is ".droppy-code-dev" in a development build (bundle id iordv.droppycode.dev) else ".droppy-code". So the shipped layout is ~/Library/Application Support/Droppy Code/{library.json, threads/, attachments/, wallpaper/} plus <home>/.droppy-code/{worktrees, patches} (Storage.swift:17-48).

Three different notions of "home" and "defaults" coexist and a port that unifies them changes behavior: Storage.stateDirectory uses `LoginEnvironment.homeDirectory` (Storage.swift:43) while TokenLedger's Codex scan uses `FileManager.default.homeDirectoryForCurrentUser` (flagged by R047); AppSettings, ChatThread.hydraDefaultEnabled and TokenLedger all route defaults through `CaptureRun.defaults ?? .standard` (WebsiteCaptures.defaults at WebsiteCaptures.swift:28 is a read-through to CaptureRun.defaults, so they are the same suite), but ShortcutStore writes key "keyboardShortcuts" to `UserDefaults.standard` directly (Shortcuts.swift:249, 262, 268) and is therefore not redirected during a capture run.

The notification userInfo contract spans three bundles and must be ported as one unit: thread notifications carry `["threadID": uuid.uuidString]` with request identifier == the same uuidString, one pending notification per thread (AppModel.notify); update notifications carry `["update": version]` with identifier "update-<version>" and no threadID (UpdateChecker); AppDelegate branches on `userInfo["update"] != nil` for routing and on `userInfo["threadID"]` for the silent-banner suppression.

Notification suppression is a double gate, described once in each report but never as a pair: AutoContinue.notify suppresses on `NSApp.isActive && app.selectedThreadID == threadID` (AutoContinue.swift:152), then AppModel.notify applies a broader gate `NSApp.isActive && isOnScreen(thread)` which also counts panel helpers and inline sidebar helpers, plus a hard `WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled` bail. AppDelegate then applies a third gate in `willPresent`, returning `[]` instead of `[.banner, .sound]`. All three must ship.

`RecentCache` is generational, not LRU (RecentCache.swift, per R033): at `current.count >= limit` or `currentCost > costLimit - cost` the whole current map becomes `previous` and current is emptied, so effective findable capacity is up to 2x limit and a read that hits `previous` promotes and is therefore mutating. Every cache in this family is one of these - ThreadRuntime.turnDiffs(limit 64) and revisionDiffs(limit 4), DocumentPrefetch.ready(limit 12, costLimit 16 MB), ThumbnailCache.thumbnails(120, 32 MB), ThumbnailMemory.images(120, 16 MB) - and R008 and R047 both describe them by "limit" alone.

Em-dash flattening happens on at least three passes and a port that implements it once will double-clean or miss: Storage.readDocument maps every loaded item through `cleanedOfEmDashes` (Storage.swift:79), ThreadRuntime's `install(_:)` normalizes again at load, and ThreadRuntime flattens streamed message/reasoning/plan deltas and provider-supplied titles live. TimelineItem.cleanedOfEmDashes rewrites only assistant text, reasoning text and plan markdown (R030); tool output, user text and notices are left alone. The exact replacement set is U+2014, U+2015, U+2E3A, U+2E3B -> ASCII hyphen, with U+2013 en dash deliberately kept (Text.swift, per R033).

Persisted state written outside the Application Support folder that a Windows port has to relocate explicitly: UserDefaults keys "keyboardShortcuts" (raw NSEvent.ModifierFlags bit values plus macOS virtual key codes - R030 flags this as a persisted AppKit constant), "appUpdater_pendingRelaunchVersion", "updateChecker_release"/"updateChecker_lastChecked"/"updateChecker_notifiedVersion", "migratedFromEarlierName", "droppycode.tokenActivity.liveDaily", "droppycode.tokenActivity.codexFiles", plus every AppSettings key; and JSON state files beside library.json (token-activity-live-v2.json, token-activity-codex-v3.json) with v1/v2 predecessors that are deleted or migrated on load.
contradictions: R008 feature note: "A session ID is held in unsentSessionID until the first message actually goes through it, so a warmed session replaced before sending never leaves an unresumable ID on the thread." Source contradicts this for API-key providers: ThreadRuntime.swift:1490 writes `app.updateThread(threadID) { $0.providerSessionID = sessionID }` directly in the DeepSeek/Meta/Z.ai branch, bypassing `recordSessionID` (1570-1577) entirely. The hold-back exists only on the CLI path (1567) and in the `.sessionReady` handler (2082).

R033 says Shell's `excludedKeys` has 13 entries; Shell.swift:331-335 has 15 (the report's own enumerated list also has 15). R033 says `readers` has 51 entries; Shell.swift:144-151 has 52 (the report's own list also has 52).

R033 says SimpleDiff's 200_000 cap is "the same cap [that] bounds command diffs in ThreadRuntime.fileEdits". They are two separate constants with different operands: Text.swift:81 `SimpleDiff.diffLimit` is compared against `old.utf8.count + new.utf8.count` (Text.swift:101), while ThreadRuntime.swift:3366 `editDiffLimit` is compared against the produced `diff.utf8.count` (3373, 3397). R008 describes editDiffLimit correctly, so the two reports disagree about whether one constant or two exist.

R003 (AppDelegate) states the capture-run early return happens "before showMain, openThreadOnLaunch, the tour, bootstrap, update checks and the relaunch marker" and calls it a short-circuit of "the entire normal launch". AppDelegate.swift:9-11 shows the notification-center delegate assignment and `model = windows.model` both execute first, and applicationWillTerminate is untouched by the flag.

R007 states that outcomes "drives the wording the notice row shows after the wait ends (.cancelled / .handedOff(newThreadID) / .resumed), per the doc comment on LimitOutcome", implying the wording is unknown. LimitResumeBadge.swift:52-60 shows `.handedOff` is matched without binding its UUID and all three produce fixed strings; the new thread's id is never used by the row, so R007's implication that the id feeds the wording is wrong.
thin_reports: R008 - 32 KB of findings for a single 3637-line file (ThreadRuntime.swift), roughly a third of the finding density of R030 (58 KB / 1680 lines) or R033 (52 KB / 1588 lines) for far simpler code. The thinness is concentrated exactly where a port is most exposed: the 117-line ProviderEvent switch (2079-2195) gets no per-case treatment at all, the two session-start branches (1430-1567) are summarized as one, and single-purpose methods that mutate persisted state (resolve's plan-state write at 1685-1695, handleLocalCommand's recordCommand at 1143/1147, interrupt's .starting path at 1664-1668, startTurn's three implicit enqueues at 1159-1167) are listed in key_symbols with no behavior recorded. The Hydra material is proportionally well covered, which suggests the reader ran out of budget on the non-Hydra half rather than skipping the file.

verdict: NEEDS_REREAD — the reports are mostly accurate and specific, but R051/R052 mis-classify two never-written environment flags (so one described rendering path is unreachable in this checkout and the shipped path is hedged as "undetermined"), R052 paraphrases the bare-domain regex and TLD table the contract demands verbatim, and R010/R015/R016 leave several user-visible strings, a revert-visibility rule and the changes-popover lifecycle unrecorded.
gaps: R016 / EffortSlider.swift:500-503: the pair caption strings are never recorded. Source is `if let headsEffort { return "The lead's effort · heads run at \(headsEffort) effort" }` and `return "The lead's effort · heads keep their own"`. headsEffort = `ModelOption.effortTitle(pair.workerEffort ?? resolvedHeadsEffort).lowercased()` (EffortSlider.swift:494), where resolvedHeadsEffort = `model.hydraLaunch(for: thread)?.workerEffort` (EffortSlider.swift:193). The caption also renders only when `pair != nil && !efforts.isEmpty` (EffortSlider.swift:637), a condition R016 omits. R016 only says "Pair caption line: font 11 secondary, lineLimit 1, minimumScaleFactor 0.9, padding .top -6".

R016 / EffortSlider.swift:531-534: `private var title` returns the literal "Standard" when `efforts.isEmpty`, and that title button still renders (EffortSlider.swift:570) above the "This model has one reasoning level." line. R016 documents the body text but never the "Standard" title, so a port would show an empty or wrong title for single-level models.

R016 / EffortSlider.swift:729-738: the mapping from state to TrackLook.Kind is unstated. Source: `switch (isMax, fastMode) { case (true,true): .fusion; case (true,false): .supercharged; case (false,true): .fast; case (false,false): .plain }` with `isMax = count > 1 && index == count - 1`. R016 gives every kind's fill/glow/spark colours but never says which slider state selects which kind.

R016 / EffortSlider.swift:331 and 363-367: the model list's detail lines are undocumented. A model row's detail is `locked ? "New chats only" : (showsProviders ? entry.provider.displayName : nil)`; a pair row's is `[modelsTitle (only when pair.customName != nil), HydraPairSummary.providers(pair), HydraPairSummary.efforts(pair)].compactMap{$0}.joined(separator: " · ")`. R016 lists `detail(for: HydraPair)` as a symbol but never its composition or separator.

R016 / FollowUpQueueTab.swift:401: the reorder gesture's own parameters are missing: `DragGesture(minimumDistance: 1, coordinateSpace: .global)` with `.updating($isGrabbing)`. R016 gives the settle maths (fallbackHeight 32, pairBand 0.25) but not the gesture that feeds it, and not the cursor-stack balance contract (openHand pushed on grip hover :389, closedHand pushed on first dragChanged :233, pop in dragEnded :294, compensating pop in `.onChange(of: isDragged)` when the row was released away from the grip :398, pop in onDisappear :392).

R009 / ChatView.swift:1395, 1407, 1502, 1513: the four in-flight git activity labels shown as the BranchMenu's own title are never recorded: "Switching", "Creating", "Pushing", "Opening pull request", set and cleared by `GitStatusModel.perform(_:_:)` (ChatView.swift:1319-1328, `defer { self.activity = nil }`). R009 states the title is `git.activity ?? git.status?.branch ?? "Detached"` but leaves the literals out.

R009 / ChatView.swift:1142: the Hydra button is gated on `model.settings.hydraEnabled, !thread.isHelper`. R009's persisted_fields records only hydraEnabled, so the rule that a helper thread never shows the button is lost.

R009 / ChatView.swift:106-109: the minimap condition is `!scene.dockedSides.contains(.leading) && (paneSize == .zero || paneSize.width - scene.reserve.leading - scene.reserve.trailing >= 900)`. R009 reports only the >= 900 branch and drops the `paneSize == .zero` case, so a port would hide the rail on the first frame before the pane is measured.

R015 / ComposerView.swift:19-49: the changes-popover lifecycle is entirely undescribed. `@State diffPopover = DiffPopoverCoordinator()`; `diffPopover.sync(isVisible: runtime.isDiffVisible, runtime:)` fires `.onAppear`, on `runtime.threadID` change and on `runtime.isDiffVisible` change; `diffPopover.reopen(runtime:)` on `runtime.diffOpenRequest`; `.close()` on `.onDisappear` and whenever the `chatColumnIsShown` environment value turns false; the tab supplies `setAnchor($0)` while the area background supplies `setFallbackAnchor($0)`. R015 mentions the coordinator only in calls_into.

R015 / ComposerView.swift:826 vs :343: the report never says which control does what. The send button while running calls `runtime.interrupt()`; Escape calls `runtime.takeBackRunningTurn()` (which returns the words to the box); Return while running calls `runtime.interruptAndSend()`. R015 lists all three calls in side_effects without binding them to their controls, so the port cannot tell the stop button from the take-back.

R015 / ComposerView.swift:310-329: the key precedence while the suggestion list is open is only half described. Source: `.up`/`.down` move `suggestions.selected` (clamped), `.tab`, `.submit` and `.steer` all call `pick(suggestions.items[suggestions.selected])`, `.escape` sets `dismissedSuggestions = true` and clears the state, `.deleteAtStart` returns false and falls through. R015 records only the escape case, so Tab/Return-picks-the-selection is unstated.

R010 / ThreadTimeline.swift:162-166: the rule that decides whether revert/edit controls exist at all is unreported: `if supportsRewind && !runtime.isRunning { rewindable = Set(runtime.turns.lazy.map(\.id)) } else { rewindable = [] }`, fed into `RowContext.canRewind`. R012 only sees the resulting `canRevert` flag, so nothing in this family states that the edit pencil and the turn-card Revert button vanish while a turn runs or on a provider without rewind support.

R010 / ThreadTimeline.swift:2236-2256: WorkingBlockView's second mode is unreported. With `earlierEntries` non-nil (a segment split off by a Hydra note, or a turn with no end marker) the same WorkingIndicator renders with `startedAt = earlierEntries.first.item.date`, `finishedAt = earlierEntries.last.item.date`, `thinkingSteps = []` (thinking is suppressed outright) and the "Earlier steps" label. R010 lists WorkingBlockView's symbols but describes only the live mode.

R010 / ThreadTimeline.swift:131-137: the empty state's side effects are missing: `NewThreadPrompt(...).onAppear { scrollChrome.update(travel: 0); scrollState.showsJumpButton = false }` resets the chrome scroll travel and hides the jump button.

R012 / TimelineRows.swift:1708 and 2624: the reveal-the-end hook has four call sites, not two. ToolRow's inline-output expansion (`if expanded.wrappedValue { revealBox?.action() }`) and TurnFinishedBlock's expansion (`if isExpanded { revealBox?.action() }`) also request it, alongside WorkGroup (:1481) and WorkSteps (:1537). R012 says only "expanding either a group or the fold".

R012 / TimelineRows.swift:1481,1537,1708,2624 vs ThreadTimeline.swift:321-322, 2089: R012 collapses `TimelineRevealBox.action()` and `.follow()` into one "revealTimelineEnd action". They are two different closures with different scroll behavior (`action = revealEnd`, held back while the jump button is up; `follow = followEnd`, reveals anyway). Every row in TimelineRows uses `action()`; only the WorkingIndicator chevron uses `follow()`.

R052 / MarkdownView.swift:750-767: the bare-domain autolinker is paraphrased where the contract demands verbatim. The regex is never given: pattern `(?<![A-Za-z0-9@._/-])((?:[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9-]*[A-Za-z0-9])?\.)+[A-Za-z]{2,24})(/[^\s<>()]*)?` with options `[.caseInsensitive]`. The `bareDomainTLDs` set is described as "comprehensive list of gTLDs and ccTLDs, 'com'..'pe'" instead of its ~115 literal entries (com, org, net, edu, gov, mil, info, biz, io, ai, app, dev, co, me, xyz, site, online, store, shop, tech, cloud, tools, blog, fm, gg, so, tv, live, news, studio, design, social, works, codes, run, page, link, chat, bot, art, fun, space, world, email, group, team, digital, agency, solutions, software, systems, network, media, photo, video, games, zone, city, life, one, plus, pro, then the ccTLDs nl...pe). A port cannot reproduce linkification from the paraphrase.

R012 / TimelineRows.swift:293 and 1116: the help string is conditional, not fixed. Source is `.help(details.isEmpty ? "" : "Show the message")` on HydraReportRow and `.help(outcome.details.isEmpty ? "" : "Show the message")` on HydraMergeRow; R012 records an unconditional "Show the message".

R015 / AttachmentFlight.swift:55: `fly(...)` returns before calling `onLanded()` under reduce motion and also when `image.cgImage(...)` or `NSScreen.main` is nil (:60-61); the armed drop has already been consumed by `AttachmentDrops.shared.take()` at the call site (AttachmentFlight.swift:195). R015 says only "fly() returns immediately with no animation when reduce motion is on" and does not state that the completion is dropped, which matters for any port that hangs chip visibility off it.
contradictions: Unreachable path presented as shipped behavior, and the two reports disagree about it. R051 (LinkParagraphView) states as fact: "passesProseThrough = !markdownBlockSelection: inside a finished reply hitTest returns nil over prose so SwiftUI's whole-reply drag selection takes over". R052 states `markdownBlockSelection` defaults true (MarkdownView.swift:877-880, MarkdownBlockSelectionKey defaultValue true). A repo-wide search shows the key is never written anywhere in the checkout (only reads: LinkParagraphView.swift:30 and :37, MarkdownView.swift:889), so `passesProseThrough` is always false and R051's prose-pass-through behavior is unreachable as shipped. One of the two must be re-read and re-classified.

R052 (MarkdownView) leaves markdownProseRuns "could not be determined from the assigned files" while R052 (ProseRunView) asserts ProseRunView is "the non-streaming alternative ... chosen when markdownProseRuns is true". The flag defaults true (MarkdownView.swift:881-884) and is never written anywhere in the checkout, so the ProseRunView AppKit path is the only path finished replies ever take and MarkdownBlockView's per-block stack runs only while streaming. Presented as undetermined in one place and asserted conditionally in the other, neither report states the settled consequence.

R012 describes the row-expansion reveal as one mechanism ("calls the revealTimelineEnd action so the view scrolls to keep the end in sight"), while R010 documents TimelineRevealBox as two distinct closures where `action` deliberately holds back when the jump button is up and `follow` does not (ThreadTimeline.swift:321-322). The code confirms R010: TimelineRows only ever calls `action()`, ThreadTimeline.swift:2089 is the sole `follow()` caller.
cross_cutting_findings: Five unresolved_questions across R009, R010 and R011 ask for TimelineMetrics' literal values; R012 has them from the source of truth, TimelineRows.swift:8-27: rowSpacing 20, hoverLineHeight 22, iconWidth 16, iconSpacing 8, pillLeading 12, pillTrailing 14, pillVertical 8, pillRadius 18. The whole family's pill geometry (ChatBadge, LimitResumeBadge, WorkingIndicator, NoticeRow, TodoListRow, merge and head pills) derives from these six numbers plus the fixed 96-point trailing gutter and the 820-point content column.

R015 and R016 both leave Storage.attachmentLimit unresolved. It is 8 (DroppyCode/Services/Store/Storage.swift:153). It caps ComposerView.maxAttachments (ComposerView.swift:137), disables PromptEditor's Add files button (PromptEditor.swift:87), and is interpolated into the three overflow notices ("... a message holds 8 attachments").

R015 and R016 leave ThreadChangesTab.overlap unresolved; R017 has it: 14 (ThreadChangesTab.swift). It is the negative VStack spacing in ComposerArea (ComposerView.swift:27), the extra bottom padding on both tabs, and FollowUpQueueTab.overlap is a straight alias of it.

R015's unresolved about AttachmentPreviewSlot vs AttachmentPreviewCoordinator is settled: they are two distinct types in DroppyCode/UI/Common/AttachmentPreviewPanel.swift (Coordinator at line 20, an NSPopoverDelegate; Slot at line 259). Neither is a typealias of the other, so the port needs both.

R052's unresolved "LinkTextVeil has no call site within the assigned four files" is answered by R051's bundle: LinkTextView owns `let streamVeil = LinkTextVeil()` and LinkParagraphView calls `streamVeil.update(view, active: markdownVeiled)` after every render and `streamVeil.detach(view)` in dismantleNSView. Symmetrically, R051's unresolved "who calls HydraHeadHoverPopover.show()/hide()" is answered by R052's bundle: MarkdownView's InlineText and ProseRunView, both on `.onContinuousHover`.

Because markdownProseRuns is always true, ProseRunView's rendering is what a reader sees for every finished reply: ballot-box task markers (U+2611 / U+2610), bullet U+2022 at depth 0 and U+25E6 deeper, no quote capsule rule, plain label colours. MarkdownBlockView's accent-coloured circles, capsule quote rule and SF-Symbol task markers appear only while a reply streams. R052 flagged the visual difference as possibly unintentional; for the port both renderings must exist and must switch on isStreaming.

Popover dismissal is implemented the same way five times and must be ported as one mechanism: an NSPopover with `behavior = .applicationDefined`, content pre-measured through a throwaway NSHostingView (fittingSize or intrinsicContentSize) and frozen with `setFixedContent(_:size:)`, plus NSEvent local monitors for keyCode 53 (Escape) and [.leftMouseDown, .rightMouseDown]. Sites: ChatBadge.BadgePopoverCoordinator, PromptEditor.PromptEditorPopover, LinkPopover (this one uses `.transient` and only an Escape monitor), HydraHeadHoverPopover (250 ms hover debounce, 300pt fixed width, 78pt height fallback), ComposerController's suggestions popover (NSSize(width: 340, height: min(340, 44 + max(itemCount,1) * 26))).

macOS primitives with no Windows equivalent, appearing across the family and needing one substitution strategy each: NSCursor push/pop stacks (TimelineMinimap, ProseRunView, MarkdownView.InlineText, FollowUpQueueTab), CADisplayLink at CAFrameRateRange(24,60,preferred 30) (StreamVeil, two clocks), CAReplicatorLayer dot fields (ComposerWorkingDots, also used by ChatBadge's attention overlay and HydraDelegationBlock's sweep), CASpringAnimation with mass 1 / stiffness 170 / damping 26 (AttachmentFlight), NSHapticFeedbackManager .alignment and .levelChange (EffortSlider drag stops, FollowUpQueueTab reorder and bundle), TextKit 1 vs TextKit 2 duality (ComposerTextView measures via textLayoutManager with a layoutManager fallback because its draw override forces TextKit 1; LinkTextView is TextKit 1 throughout).

Three separate caches key on whole message text and must be sized together in the port: MarkdownView.blockCache RecentCache limit 800, RichLink.prettyCache limit 1200, TableBlock.cellCache limit 1200, plus the fixed rings MarkdownView.streamingParses 48 slots and RichLink.streamingPretty 4 slots, TimelineBlockCache 24 threads LRU, TimelineMinimap.entryCache 400, DiffDetailCache 60, HydraDelegationBlock.readingCache 200, FileIndex.built RecentCache limit 2 with 60s freshness, FaviconCache.memory flushed wholesale at 300, LinkTitles titles flushed wholesale at 400 (with its `claimed` set never cleared, so post-flush ids can never be re-fetched).

Every editable surface keeps its edit state on ThreadRuntime rather than in the view, so the port must persist it the same way or editors will close on scroll: `runtime.messageEdit` (UserMessageRow / MessageEditor), `runtime.followUpEdit` (FollowUpQueueTab / FollowUpEditor), `runtime.followUpsCollapsed` (queue fold). All three survive the row being recycled by the lazy stack and the thread being left and re-entered.
thin_reports: R010 — 2298 lines of the family's densest control flow (scroll pinning, the AppKit nudge, blank-viewport repair escalation, phase watchdogs) summarised in the smallest report per source line of the nine (~11 bytes of report per source line, against ~21 for R009 and ~46 for R017). Its numbers check out, but it drops whole behaviors: the `rewindable` rule that governs whether revert controls exist (ThreadTimeline.swift:162-166), WorkingBlockView's `earlierEntries` mode (:2236-2256), the empty-state scroll resets (:131-137), and the distinction between TimelineRevealBox.action and .follow is stated but never tied to its callers. It also leaves six unresolved questions that other bundles of the same family already answer.

R016 — coverage is uneven rather than uniformly shallow: TrackEffect's particle, streak, bolt, sheen and fusion maths are captured to the last coefficient, while the EffortSliderCard section that a user actually reads is paraphrased. Both pair-caption strings, the "Standard" title fallback, the (isMax, fastMode) to TrackLook.Kind mapping and both list-row detail compositions are absent. The same report also hedges on a value it prints two lines apart ("28x28 -> actually 28 wide by 22 tall", EffortSlider's sibling FollowUpQueueTab.swift:383), which reads as a transcription that was not reconciled against the source.

verdict: NEEDS_REREAD - the reports are broadly accurate and unusually detailed, but R024 states a clamp backwards, R025 gets the RowDrag API and the placement fingerprint wrong and misses a glyph difference, and R048's Chrome.swift entry omits token values the whole family depends on.
contradictions: R048 documents RowDrag.settle as `settle(order:heights:fallbackHeight:pastCentre:move:) -> Bool` whose `move` closure returns Bool and gates the crossing loop (E:/Droppy/reference/droppy-code/DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/RowDrag.swift:29-35, 45, 52). R025 records the same API as `settle(order:heights:fallbackHeight:swap:)` - wrong argument label, no `pastCentre`, and no mention that the closure's Bool return stops the walk. At the sidebar call site (DroppyCode/App/Views/Sidebar/SidebarView.swift:783-793) the trailing closure's value is `withAnimation(Self.slide) { model.moveThread(...) }`, and AppModel.swift:338 / :358 declare `moveThread(_:to:placeAfter:) -> Bool` and `moveInActivity(_:to:placeAfter:among:) -> Bool`. A port that makes the move closure return Void reorders forever past a refused move.

R024 says the FloatingSidebarPanel resize is clamped 'with the minimum size as the lower bound'. FloatingSidebarPanel.swift:75-76 applies `min(max(minSize, next), area - origin - margin)`: the outer `min` runs last, so in a chat area narrower than minSize + 2*margin the written size is BELOW minSize (240x320) and is persisted to settings.sidebarPanelSize on that same drag tick (line 77). This contradicts R024's own, correct description of the read-side clamp at lines 29-32, which does use `max(minSize, ...)` on both arms.

R049 names the preferences store for "sidebarWidth"/"sidebarStartsOpen" as `CaptureRun.defaults ?? .standard`; R053 names the store for "wallpaperSoftness"/"wallpaperFile" as `WebsiteCaptures.defaults ?? .standard`. Neither says they are the same store: DroppyCode/App/Captures/WebsiteCaptures.swift:28 is `nonisolated static var defaults: UserDefaults? { CaptureRun.defaults }`. Read together the two reports imply two separate suites.

R050 describes the running breath ring as what a Hydra head at work wears (HydraGlyph.swift:21-24, `isRunning`). R025 describes the sidebar helper row as showing 'its HydraGlyph at 14 pt before the title' with no qualification. SidebarView.swift:1358 constructs `HydraGlyph(persona:size:status:)` with no `isRunning`, while SidebarView.swift:1478 in HeadCardsRow passes `isRunning: info.status == .running`. The same running head therefore breathes on its card and does not breathe on its helper row; no report records the difference.

R053's purpose line calls AppTheme a '25-case theme enum' while its own key_symbols list and AppTheme.swift:15-40 both hold 26 cases (system through matrix). The palette table in the same report also lists 26 rows.
gaps: FloatingSidebarPanel.swift:75-77 - the resize path can write and persist a `sidebarPanelSize` smaller than `minSize` (240x320) when `area.width - origin.x - 12 < 240`; no report describes that escape, and R024 asserts the opposite. Also unstated: the resize clamp is anchored on `origin` (the live `dragOrigin ?? rest`), so resizing while the panel is mid-drag clamps against the dragged origin, not the resting one.
SidebarView.swift:1358 - SidebarHelperRow's head glyph omits `isRunning`, so a running Hydra head shows no breath ring in the helper row. Unrecorded by R025 and R050.

SidebarView.swift:1872 - every thread row carries `.accessibilityValue(Text(isSettled ? "Settled" : ""))`. R025 enumerates the accessibility labels/values for SettledHeader, ActivityViewToggle, SettleCheck, the fold button and the helper stub, but not this one.

SidebarView.swift:2484-2520 - R025 calls the PlacementCache fingerprint an '18-field Fingerprint'. It has 17 fields (id, projectID, parentThreadID, isArchived, isInPanel, isSettled, settledAt, isPinned, sortOrder, activityOrder, activityOrderDay, createdAt, updatedAt, foldsHelpers, isHydraHead, hydraIndex, hasUnread), identical to ThreadPlacement's. A port sizing the invalidation key off the report gets it wrong.

Chrome.swift:178,180 - the exact glass tint on every capsule and circle in the app, `.regular.tint(Chrome.glassTint.opacity(0.3))`, is absent from R048; the report records only '.glassEffect(.regular.tint(...).interactive(), in:)'. The 0.3 is the one number that decides how much theme colour every chrome control carries.

Chrome.swift:618-646 - R048 lists `SidebarSymbol` and `SidebarIconBadge` in key_symbols but records no metrics for either, though every sidebar row, project row, badge and bottom row draws through them: SidebarSymbol is `.resizable().interpolation(.high).aspectRatio(contentMode: .fit).frame(width: Chrome.symbolSize * scale, height: ...).symbolRenderingMode(.monochrome)` with symbolSize 14; SidebarIconBadge is `.foregroundStyle(Chrome.primaryText.opacity(0.85)).frame(width: 20, height: 20)`. The 0.85 is why sidebar glyphs sit below title contrast.

Chrome.swift:1061-1069 - WindowDragView overrides `acceptsFirstMouse(for:) -> true` and swallows mouse-up with an empty `mouseUp` override. R048's side_effects mention only `performDrag(with:)`. The empty mouseUp is what stops a drag-release from reaching SwiftUI behind the sidebar.

Chrome.swift:10 sets `sheetInset = 0`, which makes every branch of RootView.swift:40-42 evaluate to zero padding: `.padding(.leading, sidebar.isVisible && !onlyFloats ? 0 : Chrome.sheetInset)`, `.padding(.trailing, 0)`, `.padding(.vertical, 0)`. R020 describes this conditional as live layout behavior without classifying it as currently inert; a port would faithfully implement a branch that does nothing today.

R049 leaves `titlebarHeight`, `collapsedTrafficLightTop` and `trafficLightsFitWidth` symbolic because Chrome is in another bundle, and R048 leaves the trafficLight* tokens as 'consumed elsewhere'. Nobody in the family closes the loop, yet these are the exact numbers a Windows custom caption bar needs: titlebarHeight = 0 + 12 + 32 = 44, collapsedTrafficLightTop = 0 + 12 + (32-14)/2 = 21, trafficLightsFitWidth = 18 + 60 + 10 = 88, trafficLightPitch = 23.

DroppyCode/Core/Support/CaptureRun.swift:10-40 - R049 and R053 both leave the defaults suite unresolved. `CaptureRun.defaults` is nil on a normal launch (everything lands in UserDefaults.standard) and only becomes `UserDefaults(suiteName: "iordv.droppycode.website-captures")` when the process is launched with the exact flags `--website-captures <folder>` or `--tour-captures <folder>`. Exact command-line flags were in scope for this read and no report in the family captured them, nor the fact that a capture run also redirects storage to `<folder>/storage` and never touches the Keychain.

settings.settledCollapsed has an undocumented default and an undocumented key. AppSettings.swift:712 reads `defaults.object(forKey: Key.settledCollapsed) as? Bool ?? true` and AppSettings.swift:133 defines that key as the string "settledSectionCollapsed", not "settledCollapsed". R025 lists the property and says it 'survives relaunch' but gives neither. The default decides that on a fresh install the whole settled list is never built (SidebarView.swift:531 `if collapsed { break }`).

settings.sidebarPanelOrigin / sidebarPanelSize persist as `[Double]` arrays, not as points/sizes: AppSettings.swift:652-672 writes `[origin.x, origin.y]` and `[size.width, size.height]` and calls `removeObject` on nil; AppSettings.swift:764-772 reads them back element-wise. R024 records only 'CGPoint?/CGSize?, nil default', so the on-disk shape and what happens to a malformed or short array are unstated.

AppModel.swift:377-379 - `settledFirst` is `(lhs.settledAt ?? lhs.updatedAt) > (rhs.settledAt ?? rhs.updatedAt)`. R025 leaves it as 'latest settled first' in unresolved_questions and never records the updatedAt fallback, which is exactly the migration behaviour for threads settled before settledAt was persisted.

R019 leaves three answerable questions open that decide user-visible strings: ShortcutStore.label(for:) is optional (RootView.swift:466 uses `if let chord = ShortcutStore.label(for: .newThread)`), and AppModel.swift:846-854 gives the palette's finish row its literal title and symbol - "Reopen thread" with "arrow.uturn.backward" when the finish action is .settle and the selected thread is settled, otherwise "<Settle|Archive> thread" with "checkmark.circle" or "archivebox". Left open, the command palette's finish row has no specified label.

KeyChord.allowedModifiers is left unresolved by both R025 and R029, yet it gates two shipped key paths: the archive popover's local monitor (SidebarView.swift:950) and ThreadWindow's Cmd-digit monitor (ThreadWindow.swift:13) and Escape close (ThreadWindow.swift:50). DroppyCode/Core/Models/Shortcuts.swift:6 defines it as `[.control, .option, .shift, .command]` - i.e. Fn, CapsLock and the numeric-pad flag are deliberately ignored.

AppTheme.swift:221-226 - `ThemeManager.current`'s didSet rebuilds spec and posts `ThemeManager.didChange` unconditionally, including when the same theme value is reassigned. R053 says it posts 'on every assignment' but does not flag that a no-op write re-tints every layer-backed spinner cell (WorkingIndicators.swift) and every HydraButton observer.

Popovers.swift:110 - `PopoverMenu` applies `.presentedChrome()` itself, so every ellipsis menu, chrome menu and picker popover carries capsule button shape and the theme tint. R048 documents presentedChrome() as a standalone modifier and as applied by setFixedContent, but not that PopoverMenu carries it.

Popovers.swift:262-273 vs :369-375 - the same RowAction runs with different timing in its two presentations. PopoverItem closes the popover first and defers `action()` into a following `Task { @MainActor in ... }` (so a sheet-presenting action survives), while RowActionMenuButtons calls `item.action()` synchronously inside the menu callback. Neither R048 nor R025 records the asymmetry, although the sidebar depends on it: the context-menu Settle posts `model.finishRequest` (SidebarView.swift:2288) while the popover Settle calls the row's own `settle()` (SidebarView.swift:2225).

SidebarView.swift:1462 and :846-849 - HeadCardsRow computes `cardRows = rows.count + (capped ? 1 : 0)`, so a head card with more than 12 heads is one glyph row taller for the chevron. The drag slot fallback in slotHeights uses `headCardHeight(rows: (headCount + 5) / 6)` and never adds that chevron row, so before the card has reported a measured height the reorder slot under-measures a capped card. R025 records the 12 cap and the headCardHeight formula but not the extra row.

SidebarView.swift:2465-2467 - `RowFrames.thread(at:)` is `frames.first { $0.value.contains(point) }?.key` over a Dictionary, so when two row frames overlap (mid-animation, or during a settle handover) the grabbed row is chosen in unspecified hash order. No report notes the non-determinism; a port using an ordered list would silently behave differently.

WindowManager.swift:76-78 - `makeCaptureWindow` uses the default `windowClass: DCDisplayCycleGuardedWindow.self`, not ThreadWindow, so the capture window has no Cmd-1..9 digit monitor and no Tab next/previous-thread chords. R029 describes it as 'the same window, at a fixed size', which reads as identical behaviour.
This family contains no protocol/IPC surface, so there is no 'protocol event handled but not reported' finding to make; the reports are correct to carry none.
thin_reports: R048 - the Chrome.swift entry is the thinnest relative to its weight: 1107 lines and the token source for every other file in the family, yet it omits the glass tint opacity (0.3, lines 178/180), all metrics for SidebarSymbol and SidebarIconBadge (lines 618-646) even though both are in its own key_symbols list, and the WindowDragView event overrides (acceptsFirstMouse, empty mouseUp, lines 1062-1068). Its unresolved_questions also park the trafficLight*, groupGap, listInset and sheetInset values as 'consumed elsewhere' when those exact numbers are what R049's own unresolved questions needed. The other eight files in R048 are well covered.

R024 - the FloatingSidebarPanel entry is 127 lines of source whose entire behaviour is arithmetic on constants, and the one piece of arithmetic that differs between the read path and the write path (the resize clamp, lines 75-76) is described backwards. Every Chrome constant it depends on is parked in unresolved_questions rather than cross-checked, so the panel's default resting origin (y = Chrome.contentTopInset = 72) is never stated as a number.
cross_cutting_findings: The whole chrome geometry resolves to literals once R048's tokens are applied to R049 and R024: sheetInset 0, chromeTopPadding 12, capsuleContentHeight 28, capsuleVerticalPadding 2 -> capsuleHeight 32; titlebarHeight 44; collapsedTrafficLightTop 21; contentTopInset 72 (= FloatingSidebarPanel's default resting y); veilHeight 72; trafficLightPitch 23; trafficLightsWidth 60; trafficLightsFitWidth 88. The Windows port's custom caption bar and floating panel need these, and no single report carries them.

Every UserDefaults key in this family (sidebarWidth, sidebarStartsOpen, wallpaperSoftness, wallpaperFile, and the AppSettings keys the sidebar reads) goes through `CaptureRun.defaults ?? .standard`, which is UserDefaults.standard on a normal launch. The alternate suite "iordv.droppycode.website-captures" is only selected by the launch flags `--website-captures <folder>` / `--tour-captures <folder>` (CaptureRun.swift:10-40), which also redirect storage to `<folder>/storage`. A port needs one settings-store indirection with the same two entry points, not per-feature stores.

Four independent window-level overlays draw in the same named coordinate space "droppy-code-window", established once at RootView.swift:68: GenieLayer (archive flights and Hydra panel morphs), RowGlideLayer (settle/reopen ghosts), CommandPalette and FloatingSidebarPanel. RootView measures the sidebar list frame in that space (SidebarView.swift:307 `windowFrame`) and SidebarThreadRow measures its own row in it (SidebarView.swift:1901). The port needs one window-level overlay host with a single shared coordinate origin, or none of the settle, reopen or archive animations can be aimed.

Reduce Motion is a global kill switch across this family, not a per-animation nicety: Chrome.panelSlide and Chrome.settleFlight swap to easeOut 0.18 / 0.20 (Chrome.swift:97-112), SidebarLayout.slideRun drops 420ms -> 220ms (WindowChrome.swift:270), traffic-light placement drops 0.32 -> 0.18 (WindowChrome.swift:221), RowGlideAnimator.launch refuses to fly at all (RowGlide.swift:76), GenieAnimator.launch and morph return false so the caller shows the real thing (Genie.swift:62, 81), HydraBreathRing installs no animation, the spinners freeze at their per-cell phase, and SettleGlideModifier fades in place. On Windows this is SPI_GETCLIENTAREAANIMATION, and it must be read in all nine places or the port's motion is inconsistent.

Two animations depend on rasterizing a live SwiftUI tree to a bitmap: RowGlideAnimator.render (RowGlide.swift:131-137) and GenieAnimator.launch (Genie.swift:84-87), both via ImageRenderer at `NSScreen.main?.backingScaleFactor ?? 2`. The ghost faces are re-rendered from ThreadRowFace with a deliberately different trailingClearance from the live row (SidebarView.swift:1944-1946), and MiniSpinner ships a separate `isStill: true` shapes-only variant (WorkingIndicators.swift:84-88) purely because ImageRenderer cannot capture AppKit views. Any port needs a view-to-bitmap capture with the same two-face + still-spinner discipline, or the settle/reopen/archive animations cannot be reproduced.

DCDisplayCycleGuardedWindow and DCNotificationGuard are pure macOS 26/27 AppKit exception nets (private `_postWindowNeeds*` overrides; NSNotificationCenter post swizzling) with no Windows analogue. They are load-bearing on macOS but must not be re-implemented; the port should record that every NSWindow subclass in the app derives from the guarded base only for that reason, and that ThreadWindow/SecondaryWindow behaviour is the part worth porting.

No theme in AppTheme defines a text colour. Chrome.primaryText and Chrome.secondaryText are the dynamic system colours `NSColor.labelColor` / `.secondaryLabelColor` (Chrome.swift:76-77), and Chrome.overlay(_:) is primaryText at an opacity - so every row fill, card fill, divider and panel scrim in the family is derived from the system label colour, not from the theme. The .system theme's surface is itself a dynamic NSColor resolving sRGB 1E1E20 in dark and FFFFFF in light (AppTheme.swift:180-187). A Windows port must choose its own primaryText/secondaryText equivalents before any of the 26 palettes mean anything.

Sidebar launch state and session state are deliberately separate: `sidebarStartsOpen` ("sidebarStartsOpen", default false) is the only thing read at launch and is written only from the Settings toggle, while `toggle()` and `endDrag()` persist `sidebarWidth` (default 268, clamped 210...440) from restingWidth and never touch startsOpen (WindowChrome.swift:286-370). The sidebar therefore always starts collapsed on a fresh install regardless of how the last session ended.

verdict: COHERENT - every claim I re-checked against the source held up (literals, strings, control flow, SF Symbol names, state machines), so no file needs a re-read; what is missing is a set of specific deferred constants, three unguarded destructive/re-entrant paths, and two capture-mode / cross-file call sites that the family never resolved.
cross_cutting_findings: Escape is detected by the raw macOS keyCode 53 in FIVE separate places in this family, each with a different swallow policy, and no report compares them: DiffInspector.swift:663-667 (DiffPopoverCoordinator.handleKeyDown closes and returns nil), TerminalPanel.swift:335-341 (TerminalHost closes the drawer and returns nil, but only when foregroundJobIsTheShell and no KeyChord.allowedModifiers are held and the terminal view is firstResponder), MCPKeyPanel.swift:65-71 and MCPSetupPanel.swift:86-92 (both close the panel and return nil while visible), ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:601-604 (cancels the recording, and its monitor swallows EVERY keyDown/keyUp/flagsChanged while recording). All five are NSEvent.addLocalMonitorForEvents, which has no Windows equivalent; the port needs five separate decisions, not one.

DiffPopoverCoordinator's mouse monitor is the one place that deliberately does NOT swallow: DiffInspector.swift:657-660 closes the popover on a left/right mouseDown outside the popover's content window but still returns the event, so the same click also activates its target (another turn's Review button opens that diff in one tap). A port that consumes the dismiss click breaks that flow. R018 states it; nobody else in the family generalizes it.

Four distinct AppKit top-level surfaces here, all borderless/chromeless with the same recipe: TourWindowController HostWindow (styleMask [.borderless,.fullSizeContentView], canBecomeKey/canBecomeMain overridden true, isOpaque false, backgroundColor .clear, hasShadow true, level .floating, collectionBehavior [.managed,.participatesInCycle,.fullScreenAuxiliary], isMovableByWindowBackground true, isReleasedWhenClosed false), MCPKeyPanel and MCPSetupPanel NSPanels (styleMask [.nonactivatingPanel,.fullSizeContentView,.titled,.closable], titleVisibility .hidden, titlebarAppearsTransparent, level .floating, hidesOnDeactivate false, collectionBehavior [.canJoinAllSpaces,.fullScreenAuxiliary], all three standardWindowButtons hidden), and the NSPopover in DiffPopoverCoordinator (behavior .semitransient, animates true, fixed 640x540). All rely on AppKit shaping the shadow to the window's alpha so it follows the rounded card.

Pre-measuring SwiftUI content with a throwaway NSHostingView before the window appears is used three times and is load-bearing each time: TourWindowController.maxBottomPanelHeight (layoutSubtreeIfNeeded + fittingSize.height, max across pages, so the tour card never resizes between pages), MCPKeyPanel.present (fittingSize.height.rounded(.up), floor 100, width 380), MCPSetupPanel.present (same, width 400). MCPSetupPanel additionally re-fits at runtime through onGeometryChange -> fit(height:), which moves origin.y by (oldHeight - wanted) so the TOP edge stays fixed.

Chrome.* design tokens are deferred as "defined elsewhere" by R018, R021, R022, R023 and R026, but they are plain literals in DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/Chrome.swift and should be captured once for the whole port: windowCornerRadius 26, sheetInset 0 (so the Settings detail pane has ZERO inset), sheetCornerRadius 16, trafficLightDiameter 14, trafficLightSpacing 9, trafficLightLeading 18, trafficLightTop 16, trafficLightClearance 10, chromeHorizontalPadding 14, chromeTopPadding 12, capsuleContentHeight 28, capsuleVerticalPadding 2, capsuleHorizontalPadding 12, capsuleHeight = 28 + 2*2 = 32 (computed, Chrome.swift:38), symbolSize 14, listInset 10, sectionSpacing 20, sectionHeaderSpacing 10, contentHorizontalPadding 16, rowControlTrailingPadding 10, rowButtonLabelHeight 16.

NSHapticFeedbackManager is used in three of this family's files and the shared `enum Haptics` is DEFINED in ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:482-486, not in a utilities file: ShortcutsSettingsPage (.alignment on a modifier added, .generic on a rejected chord and on Clear / Reset to default, .levelChange on an accepted chord), AboutUpdateViews (.alignment and .levelChange in startCelebrationSweep), ModelsSettingsPage (NSHapticFeedbackManager .alignment on every landed drag-reorder swap). Windows has no equivalent; the port must decide once where these become no-ops.

The Terminal subsystem's hardest macOS dependency is not SwiftTerm but TerminalStore.swift:69-77: `foregroundJobIsTheShell(_:)` reads kinfo_proc via sysctl(CTL_KERN, KERN_PROC, KERN_PROC_PID, shell) and returns `info.kp_eproc.e_tpgid == info.kp_eproc.e_pgid`, because the pty master answers no tcgetpgrp for a process it is not the controlling terminal of. This single predicate gates whether Escape closes the drawer or reaches vim/claude/less. On Windows (ConPTY) there is no process-group concept at all, so the Escape-at-prompt rule needs a different mechanism, not a translation.

The login-shell launch contract is exact and must be ported literally or replaced consciously (TerminalStore.swift:28-40): executable = LoginEnvironment.userShell(), execName = "-" + shell.lastPathComponent, currentDirectory = the project directory, environment = LoginEnvironment.current overridden with TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor, TERM_PROGRAM=Droppy Code, DROPPY_CODE_PROJECT_ROOT=<directory>, flattened to "KEY=VALUE" strings; args are [] with no command, and exactly ["-l", "-i", "-c", "<command>; exec <shell> -l"] for a script tab.

Persisted state this family writes is all AppSettings/UserDefaults with literal key names, plus two non-UserDefaults stores: MCP secrets in the Keychain (locked variables, via model.mcp.saveCustomValues) and non-secret custom-server variable values in mcp.json (the lock toggle's own help string says so: "Stored in mcp.json; click to keep it in the Keychain instead"). The update checker adds three UserDefaults keys of its own that this family reads but never names: "updateChecker_release", "updateChecker_lastChecked", "updateChecker_notifiedVersion" (UpdateChecker.swift:77-81).
gaps: DroppyCode/App/Views/Diff/DiffInspector.swift:626-632 - R018 states the order of show() backwards. The source is `guard let runtime, let target = resolvedAnchor() else { return }` THEN `session += 1` THEN `guard !popover.isShown else { return }`. R018's feature_notes say "show() guards on a resolved anchor and on the popover not already being shown, bumps session". The order matters: every show() call while the popover is already shown still increments `session` without touching `pendingSession`, so the stale-close guard in popoverDidClose (session == pendingSession) fails and that close will NOT clear shownRuntime.isDiffVisible and will NOT set popover.contentViewController = nil. setAnchor(_:) and setFallbackAnchor(_:) both call show() unconditionally when desiredVisible, so this is reachable in normal use.

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/MCPSettingsPage.swift:563-565 - a destructive path with no guard that no report flags. The custom-server ellipsis menu's `PopoverItem("Delete", symbol: "trash", isDestructive: true)` calls `model.mcp.deleteCustom(server)` immediately. It does NOT consult `settings.confirmBeforeDeleting` and shows no popover or confirmationDialog, unlike the archive deletes in SettingsView.swift:838-870 and :903-919 which both branch on that setting. R022 lists the menu item but never says the delete is unconfirmed.

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/MCPKeyPanel.swift:15-30 vs MCPSetupPanel.swift:17-25 - MCPKeyPanel.present has NO `isPresenting(_:)` re-entry guard and close() clears no presented-entry id, whereas MCPSetupPanel has both and explicitly returns after orderFrontRegardless when the same entry is already up. So a second call to MCPKeyPanel.present re-opens entry.keysURL in the browser and rebuilds the content view, and MCPServerCard.begin() (MCPSettingsPage.swift:533-539), MCPCustomRow.begin() and MCPInfoPopover's "Change the <label>..." button (MCPSettingsPage.swift:971-976) can all reach it repeatedly. R021 says only "the panel instance is reused"; neither R021 nor R022 flags the asymmetry.

DroppyCode/App/Views/Tour/TourPages.swift - R027 files as unresolved "whether anything else calls Tour.present ... (for example a Help menu item that replays the tour)". It is determinable and there are three shipped call sites plus one capture-only one: DroppyCode/App/AppCommands.swift:101-103 uses `CommandGroup(replacing: .help) { Button("Welcome tour") { Tour.present(model: model) } }`, which REPLACES the entire standard Help menu with that single item (a menu item nobody in the family describes); DroppyCode/App/AppDelegate.swift:18-19 gates on !hasSeenTour and sleeps 700 ms before presenting (R027's feature note names line 18 but omits the 700 ms delay); DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift:970 Button("Show").

DroppyCode/App/Captures/TourCaptures.swift:216-220 - a capture-only path nobody classified. It calls `TourWindowController.shared.present(pages: Tour.pages)` with NO onFinish and NO onClose, so in capture mode the tour never writes hasSeenTour, and the window is torn down by `TourWindowController.shared.close()` four lines later after a 1400 ms sleep. R027 documents only Tour.present's two-closure wiring and never mentions that the controller is also driven without callbacks. R018 flagged the analogous WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled gate for the diff popover, so the family is inconsistent about capture-mode coverage.

DroppyCode/App/Views/Usage/UsageFloatingPanel.swift:26-28 vs DroppyCode/App/Views/Usage/UsagePanel.swift:31 - the panel's `hasSomething` gate tests `usage?.fraction != nil`, but UsagePanel's `showsContext` requires `usage?.fraction != nil && usage?.windowTokens != nil` and its `if let usage, let fraction, let window` needs both. A ContextUsage carrying a fraction but no windowTokens, on a provider exposing neither plan limits nor credits, takes the non-empty branch and renders a UsagePanel that draws nothing (a 16pt-padded empty VStack) instead of the "Nothing to show for <Provider> yet." placeholder. R028 documents both predicates separately and never reconciles them.

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/ModelsSettingsPage.swift - R022 leaves AppSettings.modelListLimit unresolved. It is 15 (DroppyCode/App/AppSettings.swift:181), enforced again at AppSettings.swift:819 (`guard !modelList.contains(pin), modelList.count < Self.modelListLimit`). It is user-visible twice: the count line "<n> of 15. Click a model to set its reasoning effort and fast mode for every new chat." (line 64) and the disabled-add help "The picker holds up to 15 models" (line 362).

DroppyCode/App/Views/Usage/UsageFloatingPanel.swift - R028 leaves HydraPanel.cornerRadius and HydraPanel.stripHeight unresolved although they set the entire panel geometry and every content inset it reports. They are in DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/HydraPanel.swift:33 and :37: cornerRadius = 22, stripHeight = Chrome.chromeTopPadding + Chrome.capsuleHeight + 6 = 12 + 32 + 6 = 50. So the reported content height is measured + 58, and the empty state reports 94.

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift - R023 leaves AppSettings.defaultBackdropOpacity and the ChatZoom ladder unresolved, but both drive the reset affordances it documented in detail. defaultBackdropOpacity = 0.5 (AppSettings.swift:291; read back at :713 with `defaults.object(forKey: Key.backdropOpacity) as? Double ?? Self.defaultBackdropOpacity`), and ChatZoom.defaultIndex = 3 with stepCount = percentages.count (DroppyCode/UI/Common/ChatZoom.swift:11-13). Without these the "off stock" test abs(value - 0.5) >= 0.005 and the slider range 0...stepCount-1 cannot be ported.

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift:996-1000 - R023 records the LicensesRow resources ("LICENSE" with no extension, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, TRADEMARK.md) and says "per-file title 13pt semibold", but never gives the three user-visible titles rendered in the popover: "Droppy Code", "Third-party notices", "Trademarks". It also omits that the fallback string is built per-resource as "The <resource> file is missing from this copy of the app." using the RESOURCE name (so it reads "The THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES file is missing...", not the display title).

DroppyCode/App/Views/Terminal/TerminalPanel.swift:78 - a persisted field whose migration/out-of-range behaviour is unstated. R026 correctly names model.settings.terminalHeight (AppSettings.swift:144 Key "terminalHeight", default 260 at :722) and the drag clamp min(760, max(140, origin + delta)), but the clamp lives ONLY in the drag handler. `.frame(height: dragHeight ?? model.settings.terminalHeight)` uses the stored value verbatim, so a persisted height outside 140...760 (from an older build or a hand-edited plist) is applied unclamped and can only be corrected by dragging. No report states this.

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/AboutUpdateViews.swift - R021's persisted_fields is empty and its unresolved_questions never mention persistence, yet the whole AboutVersionPill standing machine it documents ("Up to date" / "Check failed" / "Not checked yet", line 626) and the check-row suffix ("Checked <relative>." vs "Not checked yet.", line 845) are driven by UpdateChecker.lastCheckedAt, which is a UserDefaults Date under the key "updateChecker_lastChecked" (UpdateChecker.swift:79, read at :118, written at :184 and :238). The sibling keys "updateChecker_release" and "updateChecker_notifiedVersion" are equally unnamed by anyone in the family.

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/MCPSettingsPage.swift:559-561 - the custom-server menu's "Disconnect" item does not set showMenu = false, while "Edit" directly above it does (line 557). Whether the popover self-dismisses on a PopoverItem action is therefore load-bearing behaviour of PopoverItem, and R022 records neither the asymmetry nor PopoverItem's dismissal contract. The same asymmetry exists in MCPConnectedRow (MCPSettingsPage.swift:184-192: "Show tools" sets showMenu = false, "Refresh" and "Disconnect" do not).

Localized vs verbatim Text is inconsistent across the family and nobody records it, which matters because Text("...") goes through the string catalog and Text(verbatim:) does not. In an otherwise all-verbatim usage stack, UsagePanel.swift:35 uses Text("Context window"); TerminalPanel.swift:67 and :71 use Text("No shell open in this thread") and Button("New shell"); MCPSetupPanel.swift:140 uses Text("Checking") while the adjacent status lines are verbatim. A port that treats all of these the same way will diverge wherever the catalog has an entry.
contradictions: R027 (TourPages.swift, unresolved_questions) says "Whether anything else calls Tour.present besides the first-run check in AppDelegate.swift (for example a Help menu item that replays the tour) is not determinable from this file alone", while R023 (SettingsView.swift, ui_elements) already documents the About app card's row "Welcome tour" / "The slideshow from the first launch: Hydra, the effort slider, panels and themes." with a Button("Show") that calls Tour.present(model:) (SettingsView.swift:970), and lists Tour.present(model:) in its side_effects. The family answers its own open question in a neighbouring report, and both still miss AppCommands.swift:101-103.

R023 (SettingsView.swift) describes the About app card as: icon, name, version, "Welcome tour" row, body text, license line - and separately lists AboutSoftwareUpdateSection / AboutUpdateCheckRow / AboutUpdateChromeAccessory only in calls_into. The source (SettingsView.swift:927-931 and :974-975) puts AboutSoftwareUpdateSection FIRST on the page, above the app card, and AboutUpdateCheckRow INSIDE the app card between the "Welcome tour" row and the body text. R021 describes both components in full but never states where on the About page they sit. Neither report alone gives the About page's row order.

R028 (UsageFloatingPanel) notes the strip draws the heads icon whenever headsProvider is non-nil, "unlike UsagePanel" which additionally requires headsProvider != provider, and calls out the duplicate-icon consequence - this is correct and confirmed (UsageFloatingPanel.swift:82-84 vs UsagePanel.swift:28). But the same report's ui_elements for the title capsule describes the second icon as "an optional second ProviderIcon(provider: headsProvider, size: 12)" with no condition, so the file entry's two sections disagree about whether a condition exists. A reader porting from ui_elements alone gets it right by accident; one porting from the UsagePanel rule gets it wrong.

verdict: NEEDS_REREAD - R036 is dense and mostly accurate on the small files, but Git.swift carries two outright wrong claims (an `add -A` timeout, and an unreachable error string presented as shipped UI text), omits the exact argument vectors of six shipped commands, and leaves the checkpoint commit's parentless shape, its two `phase` literals and the git/forge-CLI identity split undocumented.
contradictions: TIMEOUT, report vs source. R036 (Git.swift feature_notes) states 'default timeout 120 s, 300 s for push, fetch, pull, worktree add, the forge CLIs, `add -A` and diff.' Git.swift:164 `commitAll(message:)` runs `["add", "-A"]` with NO timeout argument, i.e. the 120 s default. Only the scratch/throwaway-index adds take 300 (lines 253, 448, 459, 484, 707). A port copying the report would give the user-facing commit path a 300 s budget it does not have.

UNREACHABLE STRING, report vs source. R036 ui_elements for Git.swift lists 'Error text surfaced to the user: "The request could not be merged."'. In Git.swift:212-226 `lastFailure` is initialised to that literal but overwritten with `result.failureMessage` on every failed attempt, and the loop `for attempt in 0..<6` always executes at least once; Shell.swift:15-19 guarantees `failureMessage` is never empty (it falls back to "The command failed with exit code \(status)."). The literal is dead code, not user-visible text. R036 did not classify it.

SCRATCH-INDEX FALLBACK, report vs source. R036 says currentTree's capture closure, 'when scratch is nil or the incremental add fails it deletes the scratch, re-seeds by copying the real index (or read-tree HEAD) and runs `add -A -- .`'. Git.swift:434-438: when `scratch` is nil the closure returns `try await captureTree()`, which builds a *fresh* `droppy-code-index-<UUID>` under temporaryDirectory and removes it in a defer (lines 471-487); it never touches the shared scratch. The delete-and-reseed path is only inside `captureTree(scratch:paths:)` (Git.swift:452-461), where `scratch` is non-optional.
cross_cutting_findings: Two git identities, never distinguished by R036. `Git.commitWork(_:parent:message:)` (Git.swift:268-272) runs `commit-tree <tree> -p <parent> -F -` with the message on stdin and WITHOUT `Self.identity`, so a head's branch commit carries the user's own git config identity. `commitTree(_:message:)` (Git.swift:668-673) and `captureCheckpoint` (Git.swift:423) both pass `environment: Self.identity`, forcing GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="Droppy Code" and GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL/GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="droppy-code@localhost". R036 lists commitWork only as a key_symbol and never states its flags or that it is the one commit path left in the user's name.

Checkpoint commits are PARENTLESS. Git.swift:423 is `run(["commit-tree", tree, "-m", "Droppy Code checkpoint"], environment: Self.identity)` with no `-p`. Contrast Git.swift:669-670 (`commitTree`) which appends `["-p", "HEAD"]` when `hasCommits()`. R036 describes commitTree's parent rule but says only that captureCheckpoint 'runs commit-tree with the message'. For the port this matters: checkpoints are root commits reachable solely through `refs/droppy-code/checkpoints/...`, so ref deletion (Git.swift:651-658) makes them immediately gc-able.

Forge CLIs run in a different environment from git. `Shell.run(tool:)` calls in Git.swift:181, 186, 191 and 215-217 pass no `environment:`, so Shell.swift:49 substitutes `LoginEnvironment.current` WITHOUT the GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 / GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 that `Git.run` (Git.swift:37-38) always sets. glab/gh/tea can therefore prompt on a terminal where git never would. R036 listed this as unresolved rather than reading Shell.swift.

Missing forge CLI throws an exact string R036 left unresolved: Shell.swift:129-131, `guard let executable = LoginEnvironment.which(name) else { throw ShellError("\(name) was not found on your PATH.") }`. That is the message a user without gh/glab/tea sees from createPullRequest and mergePullRequest.

macOS-only git resolution nobody flagged concretely. `LoginEnvironment.git` (Shell.swift:394-409) is `resolvedGit` else `which("git")` else `/usr/bin/git`; `developerGit` runs `/usr/bin/xcode-select -p` with an 8 s timeout and prefers `<developer>/usr/bin/git` over the `/usr/bin/git` shim (the comment cites 11.5 ms vs 4.5 ms per call). `which` splits PATH on ":" (Shell.swift:417). Every one of these is a Windows port decision and R036's platform_assumptions only says 'git is invoked as an executable URL from LoginEnvironment.git'.

`Git.run` never passes `outputLimit`, so every git invocation buffers stdout/stderr unbounded (Shell.swift:36-44, `outputLimit: Int? = nil`). R036's only size note is the 40,000-character truncation inside `workingChanges()`, which is a caller-side trim, not a capture bound. A binary `diff --binary` over a large tree (Git.swift:544-570) is read whole into memory.
gaps: Git.swift:409 `checkpointRef(thread:turn:phase:)` - R036 documents the ref template but never names the only two `phase` values shipped: "start" (ThreadRuntime.swift:1226) and "end" (ThreadRuntime.swift:2281). Nor does it name the persisted fields that hold the resulting ref strings, `Turn.baseCheckpoint` (set ThreadRuntime.swift:1250, read ThreadRuntime.swift:1773) and `Turn.endCheckpoint` (ThreadRuntime.swift:2282, read :1775). Migration behaviour of those two persisted strings across a rename of the ref namespace is stated nowhere.

Exact argument vectors missing for six shipped commands that R036 only lists as symbols: Git.swift:290 `fetch()` = `["fetch", "--quiet", "origin"]` (timeout 300); Git.swift:300 `changedPaths(from:to:)` = `["diff", "--name-only", "-z", from, to]`; Git.swift:260 `treeHash(of:)` = `["rev-parse", "<ref>^{tree}"]`; Git.swift:264 `commitHash(of:)` = `["rev-parse", "--verify", ref]` with an undocumented default parameter `ref: String = "HEAD"`; Git.swift:269 `commitWork` = `["commit-tree", tree, "-p", parent, "-F", "-"]`; Git.swift:294 `isAncestor` = `["merge-base", "--is-ancestor", commit, other]`. The bundle's own rule is that exact flags are the specification.

Git.swift:544-570 `diff(from:to:binary:paths:)` boundary unstated. R036 says it 'chunks pathspecs at diffPathChunk = 400 per invocation'; the guard is `paths.count > Self.diffPathChunk`, so exactly 400 paths is a single call. More importantly `paths: []` (non-nil, empty) still prepends `--literal-pathspecs` and appends a bare `--`, producing a full-tree diff, with no early return of the kind `resetIndex` (Git.swift:392), `checkoutPaths` (:398), `removePaths` (:403), `restore` (:602) and `previewRestore` (:577) all have. Shipped callers guard (AppModel+Hydra.swift:726, ThreadRuntime.swift:3289), so this is unreachable today, but the port needs the rule written down.

R036's unresolved_question 'isBuildOutput has no call site inside this bundle' is answerable: seven shipped call sites, all silent filters that drop the path with no user-visible report. AppModel+Hydra.swift:251 (`!isBuildOutput(path) && projects.contains { relative(...) != nil }`), AppModel+Hydra.swift:754, AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:144, :503, :530, ThreadRuntime.swift:3288, :3347. Nothing surfaces 'this file was excluded', which is a port-visible behaviour decision.

`TouchedPaths.matches` - R036 documents the suffix-matching rule but not where it is consumed: DiffInspector.swift:144 (`focus.isEmpty ? [] : files.filter { matches($0, touched: focus) }.map(\.id)`, which drives which diff rows are auto-expanded) and DiffInspector.swift:167-168 (a turn is skipped when neither `files` nor `missing` matches). The loose suffix rule therefore decides UI focus, not just accounting.

R036's unresolved_question on `previewRestore` path spaces is answerable: ThreadRuntime.swift:1776 binds `Git(thread.worktreePath ?? project.path)` and `paths` are `Set(removed.flatMap { $0.touchedPaths ?? [] }).sorted()` (repository-relative, produced through `TouchedPaths.relative`, e.g. ThreadRuntime.swift:2290, :3265). `previewRestore` itself calls `repositoryRoot()` (Git.swift:582) before the blob lookups, so the two spaces coincide only while the project path IS the repository root; a project opened at a subdirectory of a repo is the untested case, and nothing in the code guards it.

R036's unresolved_question on forge cases is answerable: MergeRequestLink.swift:6-11 declares exactly three, `.gitlab`, `.github`, `.gitea` (the comment names Forgejo and Codeberg as tea's family). It also carries a user-visible literal R036 never reaches: `var label: String { forge == .gitlab ? "!\(number)" : "#\(number)" }` (MergeRequestLink.swift:18), and URL parsing keyed on the path segments "merge_requests", "pull" and "pulls" (:25-31).

WorkingTreeWatch.swift teardown asymmetry unflagged. `shared(for:gitDirectory:)` carries an explicit comment (lines 96-98) that tearing down the *registered* watch 'stopped its stream and deleted the scratch index a capture may be writing through'. But the cookie-timeout path, `guard arrived else { tearDown(); return nil }` (line 271), calls the same `tearDown()` (lines 157-170, which does `try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: self.scratch)`) on a watch that may have `state.capture` in flight. R036 describes both paths separately and never notes that the hazard the registry path documents is unguarded here.

WorkingTreeWatch: a watch torn down by the cookie timeout stays in the `watches` registry (nothing removes it; only the `limit = 32` eviction in `shared` does, line 102). `state.stream` is nil forever after, so `settledGeneration()` returns nil at line 244 and every later `currentTree` for that directory takes `capture(nil, nil)`. R036 says 'every later snapshot is a fresh capture' but not that the dead watch is permanently sticky per directory and never rebuilt.

Git.swift:31-48 `run(_:environment:input:timeout:)` merges the caller's `extra` LAST (`environment.merge(extra) { _, new in new }`), so a caller could override GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT / GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS. No shipped caller does (only GIT_INDEX_FILE is ever passed), but R036 states the two variables as 'always set on git' without the precedence rule.

DiffParser.swift:92-93 - the `--- ` branch is consumed for every `--- ` line, and only the exact string `"--- /dev/null"` has an effect; the old path on a normal `--- a/foo` line is discarded (oldPath is set only by `rename from `). R036's prefix-dispatch list reads as if only `--- /dev/null` reaches that branch, so a port could be tempted to parse oldPath from `---`.

RevertPreview.swift:50 - the outer `numstat.split(separator: "\0")` uses the default `omittingEmptySubsequences: true`, so empty numstat text yields zero files and no throw, while each *entry* is split with `omittingEmptySubsequences: false` (line 51). R036 states the inner flag but not the outer one, and that asymmetry is what makes a trailing NUL harmless.

verdict: NEEDS_REREAD — the raw facts are unusually reliable (all 239 reported sha256 digests re-verified byte-for-byte, every lines_total correct, every ranges_read covering line 1 to the last line, and the Resources tree fully covered with no file missing and none invented), but R006 never classifies the shipped/debug status of the capture subsystem it read, and a handful of cross-file reconciliations were left as open questions that the source settles outright, two of which are live defects a port would faithfully copy.
cross_cutting_findings: SHIPPED-IN-RELEASE, unstated by anyone: DroppyCode/Core/Support/CaptureRun.swift has no `#if DEBUG` or any other compile condition, and `grep -rn '#if' DroppyCode/App/Captures` returns nothing. AppDelegate.swift:12-13 (`if WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled { Task { await WebsiteCaptures.run(model: windows.model) } }`) and DroppyCodeApp.swift:14 (`WebsiteCaptures.prepare()`) call it unconditionally. So `--website-captures <dir>` and `--tour-captures <dir>` (CaptureRun.swift:12) are live flags in the signed, notarized Release app, and the whole ScreenCaptureKit/AVFoundation stack in WebsiteCaptures.swift (1122 lines) is linked into every shipped binary.

Capture-run isolation contract, for the port: when either flag is present, Storage.swift:20 redirects the store to `<outdir>/storage`, TokenLedger.swift:87 and ProviderRegistry.swift:161 read `CaptureRun.defaults` (suite `iordv.droppycode.website-captures`, wiped at every run), APIKeychain.swift:14 returns `""` for every provider key and MCPKeychain.swift:12 returns nil, ProviderRegistry.swift:538/:669/:703 short-circuit, and UpdateChecker.swift:133 refuses to start background checks. R002's open question about the three bundled resources is resolvable: DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift:997-999 declares the tuples ("Droppy Code", "LICENSE"), ("Third-party notices", "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES"), ("Trademarks", "TRADEMARK") and line 1033 loads them with `Bundle.main.url(forResource: file.resource, withExtension: file.resource == "LICENSE" ? nil : "md")`. The whole release-artifact naming chain is one literal, reused in five places, and no report draws it end to end: project.yml `MARKETING_VERSION: "1.6.0"` -> release.sh:19-20 `Droppy-Code-$VERSION.dmg` -> publish_release.sh tag `v$VERSION` and GitLab asset `direct_asset_path=/Droppy-Code.dmg` -> netlify.toml:11-15 `/download/latest` 302 to `.../releases/permalink/latest/downloads/Droppy-Code.dmg` -> and, separately, UpdateChecker.swift:69 `https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects/86415974/releases?per_page=20`, which picks the newest stable release that ships a disk image. Break the `/Droppy-Code.dmg` asset path and both the website button and the in-app updater break.

Keychain layout: APIKeychain.swift stores every native provider key under one service, `AppInfo.name` ("Droppy Code" / "Droppy Code Dev"), with `kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked`, and only four accounts exist (CommandCodeKeychain/DeepSeekKeychain/MetaKeychain/ZaiKeychain). MCPKeychain.swift:7-8 uses the SAME service with accounts formatted `"MCP " + server + " " + field`. scripts/sync_dev_data.sh:49 mirrors only the four API-key accounts.

Tour page count, which R001 left unresolved: DroppyCode/App/Views/Tour/TourPages.swift:4-13 declares exactly 8 TourPage entries (tour-welcome, tour-hydra, tour-pairs, tour-slider, tour-threads, tour-recipes, tour-panels, tour-themes), matching the 8 tour-* imagesets in R035 and index.html's "Eight pages of real screenshots". No entitlements file exists anywhere in the repository (`find . -name '*.entitlements'` is empty) and no checked-in Info.plist (GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE = YES with only three INFOPLIST_KEY_* values). release.sh signs the DMG at line 106 with `codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --timestamp "$DMG"` and never passes `--entitlements`; the exported app is signed by xcodebuild from an ExportOptions.plist with only method/teamID/signingStyle/signingCertificate. The app therefore ships hardened-runtime with the empty default entitlement set and no App Sandbox, which docs/audit-2026-09-15.md records as deliberate ("no sandbox because the CLIs need it off").

thin_reports: R006 — not thin in volume (it captures literal UUIDs, timing offsets, pacing in milliseconds, popover widths and every mock string), but thin where it matters most for the contract: it reads the entire capture subsystem and never classifies it as shipped, debug-only or dead.
