verdict: Independent critics over the 41 re-read bundles of the 119 files that changed or were added between B1 (1.6.0) and B2 (1.6.2).
gaps: DroppyCode/App/AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:221,226,238,287,308,314,322 - The persisted HydraMergeRecord.detail strings are never quoted. The report quotes only the generic catch detail (line 360). The record detail is not the note body. It is title(...) + ": " + a shortened body, which gives doubled punctuation such as "Hydra did not merge: no remote.: The team's work is in the checkout; there is no origin to push it to." (221) and "...a rebase or merge is underway.: The team's work is in the checkout; finish that first and merge by hand." (226). The conflict detail stops at "... conflict markers from a head's landing." with no "Resolve them, then ask for the merge again." (238). The moved detail is only "A commit landed on `<current ?? target>` while the team's work was being prepared." (287). The MR-create failure detail is title + ": " + error (308). The no-URL detail is the title alone, with no colon (314). The merge failure detail is title + ": " + error, and its record carries label: link.label and url: url (322). Every failure record has files: 0.

DroppyCode/App/AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:807 - hydraBranchName's 6-hex suffix comes from a fresh random `UUID().uuidString.lowercased().prefix(6)`, not from the lead's id. The report says only "<first 6 of lowercased UUID>". A porter could derive it from the lead id, and then retried merges would collide on the same branch name. A new random name is made on every merge attempt.

DroppyCode/App/AppModel+Hydra.swift:205-213 - The pair's workerEffort only counts when keepsModel is true: `let pairEffort = keepsModel ? pair?.workerEffort : nil`. The report says "workerEffort = pair's workerEffort, else hydraHeadsEffort...". It leaves out this gate, and also that workerModel is `keepsModel ? pair?.workerModel : nil` (218). The scale for tempering is `providers.model(thread.model, for: thread.provider)?.efforts ?? []` (210).

DroppyCode/App/AppModel+Hydra.swift:202-203 - The heads label first resolves `providers.model(pair?.workerModel, for: headsProvider) ?? providers.defaultModel(for: headsProvider)` and only then falls back through `model?.shortName ?? pair?.workerModel ?? "the default model"`. So when the pair's workerModel is unknown, the label shows the default model's shortName, not the raw workerModel string that the report's ordering implies.

DroppyCode/App/AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:679-684 - hydraIsFinishedIdleEligible is listed but never defined. The rankedOut rule depends on it: `guard hydraIsOn(lead), let live = existingRuntime(for: lead.id)`, then `live.isReadyForHydraMerge, !live.isHydraMerging, !hydraHasPendingLanding(lead.id)`, then `return canStillMerge(lead)`. A lead with no live runtime is never eligible, so it is never ranked out.

DroppyCode/App/AppModel+Hydra.swift:751-757 - Missing: when prepareHydraPatch throws, landHydraHead returns a landing with `landing.error = error.localizedDescription`, no patchPath, no note in the lead timeline, and no landingStartedAt/landingFinishedAt stamps. Because landing.error is now non-nil, the head is then excluded from hydraUnmergedFileCount (289) and from hydraWork (HydraMerge 482-483). Its copied work silently drops out of merges.

DroppyCode/App/AppModel+Hydra.swift:944-961 - dismissHydraHeads first calls clearFinishedHydraHeads. For every finished head in the panel, that sets `isInPanel = false` and calls releaseHydraCopy, which stops the session, clears worktreePath/branch/baseTree, may write an -unlanded.patch and runs `git worktree remove`. The report describes dismiss only as panel-state resets (ui_elements) and never mentions that it releases copies.

DroppyCode/App/AppModel+Hydra.swift:638,689-697 vs 522-525 - The launch-failure retry resends through `headRuntime.draft = ComposerDraft(text: brief, attachments: [])` and `headRuntime.send()`, not through startDroppyHead. So executionStartedAt is not stamped again. executionFinishedAt was already set to .now at line 638 before the retry decision and stays set while the retried turn runs. The report lists these stamps as B2 additions but misses this interaction.

DroppyCode/App/AppModel+Hydra.swift:1106 - The orphan sweep skips a folder only when its creation date is readable and less than 600 s old: `if let born = try? ...creationDate, Date.now.timeIntervalSince(born) < 600 { continue }`. A folder whose creation date cannot be read is removed. The report says "at least 600 s old".

DroppyCode/App/AppModel+Hydra.swift:181-182 - hydraHeadsEffort returns the lead's own effort when the scale is empty: `(scale.isEmpty ? nil : (scale.count - 1) / 2)` followed by `guard let working else { return leadEffort }`. The report states the rung formula without this case.

DroppyCode/App/AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:333-335,525 - In the success note's Heads lines, `(<index>)` is the raw HydraHeadInfo.index, which is 0-based because the roster starts at 0 (Hydra.swift:402). `<task>` is `TextCleanup.singleLine(info.task, limit: 120)`. The report gives neither the base nor the 120 limit for HydraMergeHead.task.

DroppyCode/App/AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:776-785,766-769 - mergeRequestBody's "## Heads" and commitMessage's fallback both iterate `hydraTeam(of: lead.id)`. That is every non-archived head with a non-empty task, including heads merged by earlier jobs, not just this merge's heads. The " (1 file|N files)" suffix is added only when `landing` exists and `landing.files` is non-empty. "## Heads" and "## The lead's summary" are left out entirely when empty, and each is followed by a blank line.

DroppyCode/App/AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:396,410,428 - glab detail sources are not given. The pre-check gitLabAuth detail is the `glab auth status` failureMessage. After a failed retry, the detail is the `glab mr create` failureMessage (`detail: failure.failureMessage`). If `glab auth status` throws (glab cannot run), hydraGitLabAuthFailure returns nil and creation proceeds. After an auth failure whose re-check still fails but whose output no longer matches isGitLabAuthFailure, control falls through to the --recover check.

DroppyCode/App/AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:570-575 - The sweep's "already dirty" set is `git.changedPaths(from: "HEAD", to: base)`, which compares the current HEAD with the first unmerged turn's baseCheckpoint. It is not the dirty set at checkpoint time. Once HEAD has moved since the checkpoint, files committed in between also count as "theirs". The report's wording "not already dirty at that checkpoint" hides this. The whole sweep is skipped silently if any of the three git calls throws.

DroppyCode/App/AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:91 - The initial stage `HydraMergeStage.gathering.words` is set without the "<project name>: " prefix. Only advance() inside mergeHydraProject adds the prefix (213-216). The report says stage words are prefixed when several projects merge, without this exception.

DroppyCode/App/AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:56 - resumeHydraMerges calls `runtime(for: lead.id)` for every eligible lead, which creates runtimes, before `ensureLoaded()`. The eligibility loop then uses existingRuntime. The report says only that ensureLoaded is awaited, not that every lead within the 3-day window gets a live runtime created. That in turn changes canStillMerge and siblingOwnedPaths (659, 706), which branch on whether a live runtime exists.

DroppyCode/App/AppModel+Hydra.swift:1025,1057 - Watchdog: the loop sleeps 30 s before its first look, so nothing is checked at start-up. `HydraWatchdog.labelled.formIntersection(toolCounts.keys)` drops heads that are no longer running. On the first look `HydraWatchdog.toolCounts[head.id]` is nil, so no head can stall before its second look (at least 60 s after start). The report leaves out all three.

DroppyCode/App/AppModel+Hydra.swift:322,325 - hydraProject matches names case-insensitively against the tilde-expanded string (`caseInsensitiveCompare(expanded)`). The swap therefore happens every time the target slot is occupied, even with free slots on the side. A porter implementing 'all n slots occupied' would shift panels where upstream swaps them.

(0..<n).first(where: { occupancy[$0] == nil }) : (0..<n).reversed().first(where: { occupancy[$0] == nil })`. Running off the far end forward wraps to the lowest free index (slot 0 side), and running off backward wraps to the highest free index. That is the opposite end from where the panel ran off, so 'matching end' is ambiguous at best.

ThreadTimeline.swift:257-278,591-599 - B1->B2 behaviour change the report misses. The initial task calls `loadEarlier(in: blocks, to: TimelineWindow.initial)`. With blocks.count <= 3 this gives `start = max(0, blocks.count - TimelineWindow.firstPaint)` = 0 and `target = max(0, blocks.count - 24)` = 0, so `guard target < start else { return }` bails out. windowStartID stays nil and historyLoadPending stays false. Until the pill is seen at `threshold: 0.1` or a minimap jump happens, the window is the sliding `max(0, blocks.count - TimelineWindow.firstPaint)`, and each appended block evicts the oldest visible one ('Show 1 earlier messages' appears). A brand-new thread hits this: the ScrollView and its .task only exist once blocks are non-empty, often with 1 block. B1 did something different: `let target = count ?? visibleCount + TimelineWindow.page; guard target > visibleCount` always set visibleCount = 24 and historyLoadPending = true on the initial task, whatever the thread length.

ThreadTimeline.swift:263-267,1789-1799 - After B2 anchors the window (windowStartID = blocks[target].id), it never moves forward, so the materialized window grows without bound as blocks are appended. The report says appends 'no longer evict' but does not state that the window is unbounded. The TimelineWindow doc comment, 'the number of live views stays bounded even for very long threads', is stale in B2. A porter reading only that comment would cap the window.

ThreadTimeline.swift:538-589 - The branch order of the onScrollGeometryChange handler is not given. TouchedPaths.swift:6-13 vs 19-29 - the report does not contrast normalize with relative. normalize does NOT trim whitespace, does NOT expand `~`, does NOT reject `://`, and uses `URL(...).standardizedFileURL`, which is lexical. relative uses `path.trimmed`, `expandingTildeInPath`, a `"://"` rejection and `(root as NSString).standardizingPath`. On macOS, Foundation documents that standardizingPath consults the file system for `..` in absolute paths and for `/private` prefixes. So `normalize("~/x", root: r)` yields the literal `"~/x"` (a relative component under root), and when path == root normalize returns the absolute root path while relative returns nil. The two functions can give different answers for the same input. A port that shares one normaliser between them breaks parity.

TouchedPaths.swift:10, 26-27, 57 - platform_assumptions says a Windows port needs "case-insensitive comparison for NTFS". Upstream compares case-sensitively (`full.hasPrefix(prefix)`, `path.hasPrefix(prefix)`, `touched.contains(path)`, `hasSuffix("/" + path)`) even on macOS's case-insensitive APFS. Case folding is therefore a deliberate divergence from B2, not required for parity. The report presents it as a need without saying so.

MCPHub.swift:398 and MCPProbe.swift:179 - reply matching uses `value["id"]?.int`. JSONValue.int (Core/Support/JSONValue.swift:83-89) is `case .int(let value): value; case .double(let value): value.isFinite ? Int(value) : nil; case .string(let value): Int(value)`. So a reply whose id is "3" or 3.0 matches request 3. The report says only 'every JSON object with an int id', and a porter doing strict numeric equality would drop those replies.

MCPHub.swift:396-404 - waitStdio stores ANY object with an int id in `replies`, including server-to-client requests (ping, roots/list, sampling) that use the server's own id space. A server request with id N is returned as the reply to client request N, and the Hub never answers server requests. The report does not flag the collision, which a faithful port has to reproduce or record as a deviation.

MCPOAuth.swift:634,673 + JSONValue.swift:83-89 - `expiresIn: json["expires_in"]?.int` accepts a JSON float (truncated) and a numeric string (`Int(value)`). The report leaves this as an unresolved question and says expires_at is written 'only if expires_in present as int', but the answer is in JSONValue.swift. Only non-numeric strings, bools, null and non-finite values omit expires_at.

MCPHub.swift:398 / MCPProbe.swift:178 - the report's CRLF question is answerable. JSONValue.parse (JSONValue.swift:15-19) is `JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: data, options: [.fragmentsAllowed])`, and a trailing CR is JSON whitespace, so a CRLF line from a Windows server still parses. The report calls this 'not verified'.

MCPOAuth.swift:347-351 - `lastError = (error as? LocalizedError)?.errorDescription ?? ...` holds the FULL description of the metadataFailed/network error thrown by fetchJSON, and `throw MCPOAuthError.metadataFailed(lastError)` prefixes it again. The user therefore sees "The server's sign-in details didn't make sense. The server's sign-in details didn't make sense. The server answered 404." or "... didn't make sense. The network didn't answer." The report says only 'fetch errors set lastError to their description', so a porter passing the raw detail would drop the doubled prefix.

MCPOAuth.swift:217-223 - the candidate path is Foundation `requestURL.path`, which is percent-decoded and strips a trailing slash but keeps "/" for a root URL. For `https://h/` the first candidate is `https://h/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/` (trailing slash). For `https://h` the path is "" and both candidates are the same URL, fetched twice. For `https://h/mcp/` the path is `/mcp`. The report writes '+ path' with none of this, and JS `new URL().pathname` differs on all three.

MCPProbe.swift:354-357 - `url.path.lowercased().hasSuffix("/api/v4/mcp")` uses Foundation URL.path, which strips a trailing slash, so `https://gitlab.com/api/v4/mcp/` matches. A port using pathname (`/api/v4/mcp/`) would not match, and GitLab 404s would become `unavailable` instead of the setup guide. The report does not mention the trailing-slash semantics.

MCPOAuth.swift:581-598 - the authorization URL is built with URLComponents.queryItems. That encoding leaves `:` `/` `?` `@` and `+` unencoded and turns space into %20, so the URL literally carries `redirect_uri=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` and `scope=a%20b`. Existing query items of authorization_endpoint are re-encoded the same way. The report raises the encoding question only for postForm; URLSearchParams would give `%3A%2F` and `+`.

MCPHub.swift:456, MCPProbe.swift:309, MCPOAuth.swift:252/721/750/774 - `URLRequest(url:, timeoutInterval:)` is URLSession's idle (inter-packet) timeout, not a total deadline. The report's 'timeout 120 s' / '60 s' / '30 s' reads as a total deadline, and an AbortSignal.timeout port would behave differently. The stdio deadlines (MCPHub.swift:394, MCPProbe.swift:117) are true wall-clock deadlines.

MCPHub.swift:465-475 and MCPProbe.swift:318-331 - `URLSession.shared.data(for:)` reads the WHOLE response body before firstSSEMessage scans it. With an SSE stream that stays open, the call waits for the server to close it or for the idle timeout; it does not return on the first data line. The report's 'first SSE data message' invites a streaming early return. Only single-line `data:` fields are recognised (MCPHub.swift:483-490), and `value["id"] != nil` also accepts `"id": null`.

MCPHub.swift:477-478 and MCPProbe.swift:332-333 - `return (session, JSONValue.parse(data))` returns nil for a non-empty body that is not JSON, so the user sees "The server sent something unexpected: empty reply." (Hub, line 431/449) or malformed("empty reply") (Probe, line 269). The report records only 'empty body -> nil'.

MCPHub.swift:437 vs 447 - the Hub records Mcp-Session-Id ONLY from the initialize response (`sessionID = posted.sessionID ?? sessionID`); later responses' session ids are discarded (`let posted = try await post(...)` at line 447, whose sessionID is never read). The Probe updates it on every response (MCPProbe.swift:249). Also, once `initialized` is true the HTTP client never re-initializes: a server that expires the session and answers 404 gives "The server answered 404." on every call until reload(). didRestart/dead apply only to stdio. The report does not state this difference.

MCPHub.swift:26,371 - `MCPHub.track(proc)` is called only from MCPClient.startStdio. MCPProbe's processes (MCPProbe.swift:122-167) are never added to MCPLiveProcesses, so `MCPHub.terminateAll()` at applicationWillTerminate (AppDelegate.swift:54) does not kill a probe that is running when the app quits. The report's 'process-wide registry of every spawned server process' overstates it.

MCPOAuth.swift:194-196 - `static func refreshIfNeeded(serverID:)` has no caller anywhere in B2. A grep of DroppyCode finds only its definition; the other `refreshIfNeeded` hits are TokenLedger. The report lists it as API without saying it is unused, so a porter may wire a proactive refresh that upstream does not have.

MCPOAuth.swift:709-712 and 394-398 - `MCPKeychain.set(...)`'s Bool result is ignored, and storeSession silently returns if serialization fails. signIn therefore completes without error even when the token was not stored, and isSignedIn stays false. The report does not record this. The stored JSON also uses JSONSerialization `.sortedKeys` without `.withoutEscapingSlashes`, so URLs are persisted as `https:\/\/...` (for example token_endpoint). That byte-level fact matters if the port must read or write the same blob.

MCPProbe.swift:246-265, 318 - transport failures (URLError) are not caught and propagate raw, so the user sees Foundation's localizedDescription (for example "The request timed out.", "A server with the specified hostname could not be found."). A non-HTTP response gives `MCPProbeError.malformed("invalid reply")` (line 320). In the Hub, `call()` wraps such an error as `MCPHubError.server(error.localizedDescription)` (MCPHub.swift:96). The report lists only the app's own strings and does not say that platform network error text reaches the UI.

MCPHub.swift:213 and MCPProbe.swift:324 - `rawDescription.prefix(400)` and `.prefix(2000)` count Swift Characters (grapheme clusters), not UTF-16 units or bytes. The report says 'first 400 characters' / 'first 2000 chars' without saying how they are counted.

MCPOAuth.swift:305-308 - `value.split(separator: " ")` omits empty pieces, so runs of spaces collapse. The report's 'splits the scope value on single spaces' could be ported as JS `split(' ')`, which keeps the empty strings.

MCPKeychain.swift:63-67 - deleteAll deletes only `entry.fields[].key`. It does not remove "oauth" or "oauth-client"; MCPStore.swift:124-126 calls `MCPOAuth.signOut` separately for that. The report does not state this split of responsibility.

MCPProbe.swift:55 - the stdio branch is chosen by `server.command != nil`, not non-empty. An empty command goes to probeStdio and becomes commandMissing(""), shown as " isn't installed. Install it, then try again." with a leading space. The report's 'command != nil -> stdio' is right but does not draw out the empty-string case.

MCPProbe.swift:177-182 - nextReply returns from inside the `for line in conversation.takeLines()` loop, so any lines after the match in the same batch are dropped for good. Unlike MCPHub.waitStdio (line 409), there is no `!process.isRunning` check; exit is seen only through terminationHandler. The report does not mention either.

MCPStore.swift:22-28 + MCP.swift:164-166 + MCPProxy.swift:111-124 - The report never gives this ordering hazard. init runs `MCPProxy.shared.start()` and then `exportAll()` synchronously. exportAll resolves every server through `server.url = MCPProxy.url(for: id)` (MCP.swift:165) with the saved port. Per the MCPProxy.swift:96-98 comment, a taken port 'fails only once the listener starts', so the `.failed` handler runs later on `queue` and calls `Self.repickPort()`. The provider configs and MCPHub written at launch then point at the old, dead port until some later exportAll (connect success, disconnect, setEnabled, saveCustom). Nothing in either file re-exports after a re-pick. A porter who re-picks synchronously before exporting would diverge, and so would one who re-exports on re-pick.

MCPProxy.swift:103 - `parameters.allowLocalEndpointReuse = true` is listed only as a side effect. The whole re-pick design (lines 8-11: 'the Dev build runs over a mirror of the release library, so both would otherwise ask for the same one, and the second to launch would answer nothing') depends on the second bind FAILING. On Windows, the literal equivalent (SO_REUSEADDR) lets a second socket bind the same port, so the collision is never detected. The report's platform_assumptions should warn not to map this flag to SO_REUSEADDR on Windows, and should rely on EADDRINUSE from a plain listen.

MCPProxy.swift:315 - `request.timeoutInterval = 3_600` is reported as a bare '3_600 seconds'. On URLRequest/URLSession this is an idle (inactivity) timeout between data, not a total request deadline. A port using fetch/AbortSignal.timeout(3600000) would kill long-lived text/event-stream responses after one hour, even while they are active.

MCPProxy.swift:376-387 + 403-408 - Consequence omitted: `send` resumes on `.contentProcessed { _ in continuation.resume() }` and ignores the error. So when the agent CLI closes its connection mid-SSE, the `for try await byte in stream` loop keeps reading the upstream until the upstream ends or times out. The upstream request is never cancelled on client disconnect. The report states that send ignores errors but not this behaviour.

MCPProxy.swift:193-202 - The divider check comes before the size check (`if let divider = buffer.range(of: Self.divider) {...}` before `if buffer.count > Self.headLimit`). Each receive is capped at `maximumLength: Self.headLimit` (65_536). So a head is accepted as long as its \r\n\r\n arrives before the accumulated buffer passes 65_536. That allows heads up to about 131_071 bytes, and the 413 'request head too large' fires only when no divider has been found. The report's wording implies a hard 64 KiB head limit.

MCPProxy.swift:389-392 - The non-SSE response is buffered with no size limit (`var payload = Data(); for try await byte in stream { payload.append(byte) }`). `bodyLimit` (32 MiB, line 50) applies only to request bodies (line 241). The report does not say that response size is unbounded.

MCPProxy.swift:344-352 - This is not stated: when the retry token fetch fails (`try?` yields nil), the ORIGINAL upstream 401 status and body are written back to the client via writeBack. Also, the first 401 `stream` is replaced without being drained or cancelled. The second `MCPOAuth.accessToken(serverID:)` call passes no force-refresh flag, so whether a new token comes back is MCPOAuth's decision. A porter reading 'retrying once on a 401' may assume a forced refresh.

MCPProxy.swift:344 and 349 - `URLSession.shared.bytes(for:)` carries URLSession.shared platform defaults that the report does not list: HTTP redirects are followed automatically, gzip/deflate Content-Encoding is transparently decoded (writeBack at lines 360-370 copies only Content-Type, Mcp-Session-Id and Cache-Control, never Content-Encoding or Set-Cookie), and cookies go to the shared cookie store. A port on raw Node http would pass compressed bytes with no Content-Encoding header and would not follow redirects.

MCPProxy.swift:100 - `guard let endpointPort = NWEndpoint.Port(rawValue: port) else { return }` returns WITHOUT resetting `running`. start() already set `state.running = true` (line 87), so every later start() is a no-op. The report says only 'returns silently'.

MCPProxy.swift:137-150 plus a repository grep - stop() has no caller in B2. The only references to MCPProxy outside the file are MCP.swift:12 (a comment), MCP.swift:165 and MCPStore.swift:26/95/101/127/282/311/326/331. The report leaves this unresolved ('Whether stop() is ever called by the app ... is not established here') when one grep answers it. Similarly, every register/replaceAll call passes `headers: [:], usesOAuth: true` (MCPStore.swift:284, 311), so the `route.headers` override (lines 328-330) and the `usesOAuth == false` path are unreachable in B2. The report does not note this.

MCPProxy.swift:15 + MCP.swift:237-241 - The report leaves MCPPaths.directory unresolved, but it is `Storage.root.appendingPathComponent("mcp", isDirectory: true)` and is created on first access (`try? FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: url, withIntermediateDirectories: true)`). So the port file is `<Storage.root>/mcp/proxy-port`. The same enum (MCP.swift:248-252) puts claude.json, codex.json and copilot.json beside it. MCPStore's report cited this enum for connectionsURL, so the location was within reach.

MCPStore.swift:4-7 - The file's doc comment names the external CLIs, and the report omits them: 'syncs the file-based CLIs (Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini)'. The same comment places the provider configs 'under `MCPPaths.directory`'. The report's purpose says only 'the file-based external CLIs (MCPExternalSync.sync)'.

MCPStore.swift:279-285 + 307-311 - Race omitted: probeOnce registers a route for a server that is not yet connected (`MCPProxy.shared.register(serverID: entry.id, upstream: remote, headers: [:], usesOAuth: true)`). But exportAll replaces the whole route table with enabled AND connected servers only (`enabledServers` filters `$0.isEnabled && $0.connectedAt != nil`, line 43). Any exportAll during that probe wipes the route of the server being probed, for example another server's probe succeeding, a setEnabled, or a disconnect. The proxy then answers 502 'unknown server' (MCPProxy.swift:289-292). A porter who keeps the route table additive would behave differently.

MCPStore.swift:245-260 - The report says 'a decode failure leaves connections empty' / 'decode failure leaves customs empty' but gives no consequence. init then calls exportAll (line 27), which rewrites every provider config and the proxy routes with zero servers. The next `save()` (line 262-269) or `saveCustoms()` overwrites mcp.json or custom-mcp.json with only the entries created since, so a single undecodable record destroys the user's saved list. Decoding is all-or-nothing over the array (`decoder.decode([MCPConnection].self, from: data)`).

MCPStore.swift:262-268 - The file-format detail is incomplete. `encoder.outputFormatting = [.prettyPrinted, .sortedKeys]` does NOT include `.withoutEscapingSlashes`, so Foundation writes '/' as '\/', for example in URL values stored in `values`. `.iso8601` encodes whole seconds with 'Z' and no fractional part, and the matching decoder (line 252) rejects fractional seconds. The report says the byte layout 'must be reproduced' but gives none of this, and a JS `toISOString()` writer (".000Z") would produce a file that fails to decode.

MCPStore.swift:103-111 - connect writes a secret draft to the Keychain even when it is empty (`MCPKeychain.set(text, server: entry.id, field: field.key)` with no emptiness check), and writes an empty plain draft as `connection.values[field.key] = ""`. saveCustomValues (line 231), by contrast, stores nil for empty plain values. The report records the empty-secret case only for saveCustomValues and misses this asymmetry.

MCPStore.swift:156-165 - Unreported: if `oldID` is given but no custom has that id, `old` is nil. The server is then treated as NEW, gets `MCPCustomServer.makeID(server.name)` and is appended, and oldID is silently ignored. The incoming `server.id` is always overwritten.

MCPStore.swift:137-141 + 335-341 - refresh does not check that a connection exists. If the probe then succeeds, `states[entry.id] = .connected(toolCount:)` is set even though `connections[entry.id]` is nil (the `if var connection` guard only skips the field update), so the card shows connected with no persisted connection. The report describes both halves separately but not this outcome. Also, finished probe Tasks are never removed from `probes` (only cancel paths clear it).

APIKeychain.swift:31,45,61 - The Keychain service is `kSecAttrService as String: AppInfo.name`, but the report never gives the literal. AppInfo.name (Core/Support/Text.swift:4) is `Bundle.main.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: "CFBundleDisplayName") as? String ?? "Droppy Code"`. A Windows Credential Manager port needs the literal target name "Droppy Code" to reproduce the service/account pair.

APIKeychain.swift:13-16 vs 22-40 - The report says key(for:) reads nothing in a capture run (`guard !CaptureRun.isEnabled else { return "" }`). It does not say that setKey has no such guard, so a capture run still deletes and writes real Keychain items.

APIKeychain.swift:4-8 - The report leaves the account strings as an open question. They sit in the four wrapper enums that still exist and call into this file: "Z.ai API Key" (ZaiKeychain.swift:6), "Command Code API Key" (CommandCodeKeychain.swift:8), "DeepSeek API Key" (DeepSeekKeychain.swift:6), "Meta API Key" (MetaKeychain.swift:6). These are the persistence keys a port must keep.

AntigravitySession.swift:91 - The report's launch-argument note just says 'then mode arguments'. The source is `modeArguments(runtimeMode: configuration.runtimeMode, interaction: configuration.interactionMode)`, which is always the original configuration's modes. Only `model` and `effort` (line 88, `Self.normalize(model: model, effort: effort)`) come from the mutable per-turn properties.

AntigravitySession.swift:259-265 - The report says finishEdit returns nil 'for non-edit steps'. It actually returns nil whenever no ACTIVE snapshot was taken: `guard let before = editSnapshots.removeValue(forKey: id), let path = Self.path(in: parameters) else { return nil }`. That includes edit steps first seen as DONE or ERROR, and edits without a path; those rows keep the placeholder `FileEdit(path:)` from makeToolCall.

AntigravitySession.swift:689-693 - The web tool list is paraphrased as 'the browser_* interaction tools'. The exact names are browser_click_element, browser_drag_pixel_to_pixel, browser_get_dom, browser_get_network_request, browser_input, browser_list_network_requests, browser_mouse_down, browser_mouse_up, browser_move_mouse, browser_press_key, browser_refresh_page, browser_resize_window, browser_scroll, browser_scroll_dom, browser_select_option, plus click_browser_pixel and execute_browser_javascript. Read as a prefix rule, 'browser_*' would wrongly include browser_subagent, which is `.agent` (line 695).

AntigravitySession.swift:666-667 - The MCP title keys are cut short. The server is `["ServerName", "server_name", "Server", "server"]` with default "MCP", and the tool is `["ToolName", "tool_name", "Tool", "tool"]` with default "tool". The report only names ServerName and ToolName.

AntigravitySession.swift:652-658 - For search without a pattern, the title falls back to the folder: `return ToolCall(kind: .search, title: folder ?? Self.humanize(name))`. The report only describes the pattern case with the folder as detail.

AntigravitySession.swift:644-645,721 - The read detail is set only when a path exists (`if path != nil, let range = Self.lineRange(in: parameters)`). "L<start>–<end>" is used only when `end > start`, otherwise "L<start>". The report states neither condition.

AntigravitySession.swift:574 - The report writes the bucket id fallback as "<group>-<index>". The source is `"\(groupName)-\(windows.count)"`, where windows.count is the running count across all groups, not a per-group index.

AntigravitySession.swift:531-532 - authStatus scans `TextCleanup.stripANSI(result.output + result.errorOutput)`, which is stdout and stderr together, and its slug-row check does not trim lines. The report mentions neither the combined streams nor the difference from listModels, which trims and reads stdout only.

AntigravitySession.swift:311-315 - The .tokenSpend event carries `model: model`: the raw last TurnInput or configuration model, not the normalized base slug that is passed to `--model`. The report does not say which one.

AntigravitySession.swift:113-119 - The 30-second timeout Task is never cancelled after a successful init. It fires later and returns harmlessly only because initContinuation is nil by then. The report does not say this.

ACPSession.swift:788-799 - The report cuts subjectPhrases short with '...' and gives only a partial verb set. Full phrase list, in order: "searched web for ", "search web for ", "searching web for ", "searched the web for ", "search the web for ", "searched for ", "searching for ", "search for ", "reading file ", "read file ", "listed directory ", "listing directory ", "list directory ", "listed files in ", "list files in ", "listing files in ". The report does not list the 54 verbs at all, from "read", "reading", "viewed" through "opened", "opening", "open" (lines 794-798); a porter needs every entry.

ACPSession.swift:592-601 - Auto-approval returns nil when neither an allow_once nor an allow_always option exists (`return (allowOnce ?? allowAlways)?["optionId"]?.string`). The request then falls through to a user approval prompt even in fullAccess. The report states only the pick order.

ACPSession.swift:498-502 - agent_thought_chunk does not clear messageID, and only agent_message_chunk clears thoughtID. A message chunk after a thought therefore continues the same message entry (`?? messageID ?? nextID("message")`). The report does not say this.
ACPSession.swift:724-726 - The search detail is set only when `pattern != nil || !title.isEmpty`, and also path != workingDirectory and path != call.title. The report leaves out the first condition.

ACPSession.swift:446 - applySelection sends `let wireID = usesParameterizedModels ? Self.baseModelID(model) : model`, so Cursor's requested model has its [..] parameters stripped before sending, and currentModel is set to wireID even if the request fails (line 453). The report states neither.

ACPSession.swift:309-318,840-847 - Defaults the report leaves out: an applyModels entry takes `name: entry["name"]?.string ?? id` and `detail: entry["description"]?.string`, and diff blocks default `oldText`/`newText` to "". makeToolUpdate sets edits only when non-empty (line 755).

ClaudeSession.swift:121-128 - The report leaves open whether `--append-system-prompt` can be empty and does not record the comment "The off notice goes out too, so a resumed thread cannot keep earlier guidance alive." In B2, AntiSlopPolicy.swift:16 is `static func instructions(enabled: Bool) -> String { enabled ? enabledInstructions : disabledInstructions }`, and the disabled text begins "[Droppy Code anti-slop guidance: off]\nDisregard earlier app-provided anti-slop guidance. ...". ClaudeSession.swift:39,477,535,552-553,591 - toolNames is one dictionary shared by the lead and every head. `toolNames[toolID] = name` is written from both the lead and the head streams, and `toolNames.removeAll()` runs at every lead `result`. Head tool results go out through `parent.map(agentSink) ?? leadSink` (line 372), which the report never states.

The report's 'isError = is_error or else subtype != "success"' can be read as a logical OR. Only the static handshake has the 20 s watchdog (lines 193-196). The report does not say that session start has no watchdog, which a Windows port must reproduce or deliberately change.

A turn that is live when the CLI dies ends only with `.exited(error: TextCleanup.lastLines(tail))`, and only if `!isStopping && isStarted`. The report's didClose note omits both facts.

ClaudeSession.swift:755-759 - MCP title fallbacks are missing from the report: `let server = parts.count > 1 ? String(parts[1]) : "MCP"` and `let tool = parts.count > 2 ? parts[2...].joined(separator: "__") : name` (tool segments rejoined with "__", split with omittingEmptySubsequences: true). Because the stream-start path calls `toolCall(name: name, input: [:])` (line 478), an MCP row first shows detail "{}" until the assistant message's `.toolUpdated` replaces it.

ClaudeSession.swift:514 / Text.swift:132 - The report leaves open what `.trimmed` does. It is answerable in B2: `var trimmed: String { trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) }`, so B1->B2 change (2) here and change (5) in CodexSession (lines 689, 698, 770, 808) change no behaviour.

cross_cutting_findings: These rules decide merge ordering, and a port must copy them byte for byte: B2 contested-file arbitration compares `uuidString` values (HydraMerge 52, 700), which Swift renders in uppercase. A Windows port that compares lowercase GUID strings, or Guid.CompareTo (which compares fields in byte order), would pick different winners. Worktree folder names and patch file names use `uuidString.lowercased().prefix(8)` (Hydra 544, 878, 1001).

POSIX path logic appears in all three places a porter must replace: hydraProject's walk to "/" (Hydra 329-340), the hydraWork anchored() absolute test `hasPrefix("/") || hasPrefix("~") || contains("://")` (HydraMerge 498, 537), and isScratchPath's roots ("/tmp", "/private/tmp", "/var/folders", ~/Library, dot-folders under home) (HydraMerge 193-205). On Windows, drive-letter paths would all count as relative and be appended to the checkout.

User-visible strings contain non-ASCII characters that must be kept exactly: U+2026 in "Settings…", "Add project…", "Archive thread…" and "Thinking for N min…"; U+00B7 in head titles; U+2014 in the merge note's Heads lines (HydraMerge 333, 335); U+2212 in filesLine and the MR body Files lines (856, 797); U+2026 in the 2,000-character cut (793). Note that the port's own rules may conflict with the em dash.

AppKit and macOS dependencies in note(): `NSApp.isActive && selectedThreadID == leadID` suppresses unread, the Dock badge and the notification (HydraMerge 868-874). Windows needs an equivalent for app-active and for updateDockBadge.

Hydra copies nest detached git worktrees under Storage.worktreesDirectory with names "<project-slug>-<persona-slug>-<8hex>" (Hydra 542-545). On Windows, path length and git's core.longpaths behaviour need checking for deep checkouts. The report does not raise this.

Helper membership is chosen differently per operation: helpers(of:) (398) for archive, settle and sidebarThreads, and children(of:) (236) for delete, reopen, unarchive (direct scan at 776) and markRead on selection (85). A port with a single "helpers" concept will break these asymmetries.

Several behaviours depend on SidebarView, outside this file: consuming FinishRequest and ArchiveRequest within the 80 ms window (867, 884, 907), the scroll to sidebarRevealThreadID, and the inline-helper visibility rule that isOnScreen copies (1147-1148 "the same condition `SidebarView` uses"). The readers of those files must confirm matching conditions.

Hydra members this file calls (sweepHydraCopies, resumeHydraMerges, runningDroppyHeads, releaseHydraCopy, finishHydraHead, hydraHeadTurnFinished, hydraPickerPairs, hydraLead) live in AppModel+Hydra.swift. hydraHeadRetries' limit of 2 is enforced there (line 682).

Path identity (addProject dedupe at 517-518, project.path used as Git root and script directory) assumes case-sensitive POSIX paths. The Windows port needs normalization rules decided explicitly and recorded as a documented deviation or equivalence.
