Swift only warns about the unreachable second arm. recordTokenSpend's merge, the hydraTokens bump and scheduleSave never run from live events. pendingNativeSpend never fills. Token counts for a Droppy head rise only when install() recomputes them. The raw arm's updateTurn (3554-3558) only bumps saveRevision; nothing schedules a save.

Hydra timing: spawnWaitingHeads (3004) writes queuedAt, and startTurn (1217-1228) writes the start, execution and landing fields only for Droppy heads after their first turn. The spawn path in AppModel must set executionStartedAt for the first turn, as the report's unresolved question says; that is outside this file.

The chatZoom -> appZoom change in B2 reaches beyond this bundle: the whole-window zoom (key "appZoom", default 100, stepped by AppZoom.next, reset by 'Actual Size') replaces per-view font scaling. Any port reader who records only 'chatZoom removed' across other R2 bundles (HydraHeadPopovers.swift and HydraReportsPopover.swift also set `.environment(\.chatZoom, 1)` at B1) risks the same omission. A porter needs the appZoom mechanism from AppSettings.swift, AppCommands.swift and SettingsView.swift (AppZoomCard).

Persisted keys differ from property names at least once ("floatingPanelSize" for panelSize). Reports that list AppSettings fields should quote the UserDefaults key strings and defaults from AppSettings.swift rather than property names.

The B2 text-style swaps (title3, title2, subheadline, body, callout) match the removed fixed sizes (15, 17, 11, 13, 12) only under macOS's fixed text-style table. A Windows port should pin these as explicit point sizes rather than map them to Windows text styles.

Across all five files, B2 swaps fixed point sizes for SwiftUI text styles, and the report leaves the real sizes open each time. Every swap keeps the macOS default size of its new style except the two 9 pt -> .caption2 cases (HydraButton.swift:630, HydraMergePopover.swift:166). One Windows type-ramp table (caption2 10, footnote 10, subheadline 11, callout 12, body 13, title3 15, title2 17) settles the question for the whole bundle and should come from a single place, not from per-file guesses.

Fixed sizes that B2 did not convert should be kept as fixed pixels, not moved onto the ramp: badge MiniSpinner cellSize 2.4, HydraNameText 12.5/13/14, the heads count `.system(size: 12.5, weight: .semibold)`, symbol sizes 18/20 in the intro and merge card, and markdownPointSize 12. The report mentions most of these, but only in scattered places.

`.environment(\.chatZoom, 1)` was removed from both head popovers, and chatZoom no longer exists anywhere under DroppyCode/ in B2. Any Windows code that ported chat zoom from B1 must be removed or re-derived from whatever replaced it. That lies outside this bundle but affects every popover in it.

The persisted flags used in this bundle (hasSeenHydraIntro, hydraShowsHeadDetails, hydraEnabled) have their keys and defaults in AppSettings.swift. Readers should cross-reference them and not stop at 'not in this file', because the default of hydraShowsHeadDetails (false) decides which stage view a new install shows.

All five files moved from fixed point sizes to system text styles (.subheadline, .callout, .body, .footnote), or to Font.chat, which is also a system text style. Scaling now comes from the app-wide appZoom (AppSettings key "appZoom", default 100, AppZoomModifier at the window roots, WindowManager.swift:172-175), not from the removed per-chat chatZoom. The Windows port should map the text styles to fixed macOS sizes (body 13, callout 12, subheadline 11, footnote 10) and apply appZoom as a whole-window scale.

Two source doc comments contradict the code: HydraProgressBar.swift:15 says '1.8 s' and lines 137-138 say the clock keeps running while scrolling; HydraReportsPopover.swift:589 says 'trimmed in the middle'. Porters must follow the code, not the comments.

The landed-file grammar relies on forward-slash, space-free paths (`\S+`, split on ", ", lastIndexOf "/"). If the Windows lead or merger writes backslash paths or paths with spaces, the report popover silently loses files. Whoever writes the lead's report message needs to know this.

The B1->B2 foreground change from `.secondary` to Chrome.secondaryText (MessageEditor, LimitResumeBadge icon) swaps a hierarchical style for a fixed Chrome token, so the port should use the Chrome token value, not an opacity derived from the parent.

B2 commit e6ec1f44d replaced `.font(.system(size: 12))` with `.font(.system(.callout))` across about 35 view files (70 additions, 72 removals under DroppyCode). The Windows port should treat this as one typography decision: callout-sized text, scaled by the whole-window app zoom (AppSettings.appZoom, AppZoomModifier). Each reader report should not interpret it separately as Dynamic Type.

PanelDockCorner raw strings are a persistence format (AppSettings key "usagePanelDock", default .bottomLeading). Any report on AppSettings or PanelScene should record them verbatim, and the port must keep the four case names byte-for-byte.

SubagentPanelLayout reads Chrome.contentTopInset, and the strip uses Chrome.chromeTopPadding/capsuleHeight/capsule* constants whose values live in DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/Chrome.swift. Docked positions cannot be computed numerically until the reader of that file supplies those values.

chronologicalTimeline is a persisted AppSettings key (default false) that nothing in B2 reads. ThreadTimeline.row hard-codes `chronological: false` (line 330), so TurnFinishedBlock and WorkingIndicator always receive false. `.onChange(of: chronological, initial: true)` therefore always sets isExpanded = false and showsAllSteps = false. For parity, the Windows port should persist the key but not wire it to the timeline. The readers of AppSettings (bundle owning AppSettings.swift) and TimelineRows.swift:2492 should check the same fact.

Font.chat is defined at DroppyCode/UI/Common/ChatFont.swift:6 as `static func chat(_ style: Font.TextStyle, weight: Font.Weight? = nil, design: Font.Design = .default) -> Font` with no zoom parameter in B2. The bundle that owns that file answers the report's unresolved question about it.

The first-paint path differs sharply from B1. The window is a sliding newest-3 until something anchors it, and B2 no longer sets historyLoadPending on short threads. Whoever ports the timeline should test three cases against upstream behaviour: a new thread growing past 3 turns, a thread reopened with more than 3 blocks, and a thread reopened with 4 to 24 blocks (anchored at block 0, so every block stays materialized).

The caller (ThreadTimeline.swift:180-195) holds facts this report leaves unresolved, and whichever report covers ThreadTimeline.swift should state them. The rail is shown only `if showsMinimap, blocks.count(where: \.hasUserMessage) > 1`. It gets `centerHeight: max(0, columnHeight - WindowChrome.titlebarHeight)`, is wrapped in `.equatable()`, and is sized `.frame(width: 30)` with `.padding(.top, WindowChrome.titlebarHeight)`. It appears and disappears with `.transition(.opacity)`, and the show/hide animation is `liveResize.isReshaping ? nil : Chrome.panelSlide`. onNavigate is `jump(to: id, in: blocks, animated: animated)`.

The report's unresolved Chrome.* values (cardCornerRadius, chromeTopPadding, capsuleHeight, accent, primaryText, secondaryText), the RecentCache eviction policy, and the WindowLiveResize isActive/isReshaping semantics all need to come from the reports on Chrome, RecentCache and WindowLiveResize. The hit-rect top clearance depends directly on `Chrome.chromeTopPadding + Chrome.capsuleHeight` (line 427).

Chat zoom was removed in B2 across the app, not only in this file. ChatFont.swift in B2 has no zoom parameter, and its doc comment says the app-wide zoom scales the window. The Windows port should apply zoom to the whole window (Electron zoomFactor or CSS zoom on the root), not scale chat font sizes. Every .chat(style) resolves to the macOS system text-style size (callout 12, caption 10, caption2 10, headline 13 semibold, footnote 10, subheadline 11 on macOS). The measured values still need confirming, as the report says.

Several pills hug their content by putting `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: ...)` AFTER `.background`, while NoticeRow puts it BEFORE. The order decides whether a background hugs or spans the row. A CSS port has to copy this per row: fit-content for pills, full width for notices.

Four ways of anchoring a popover appear in this file: badgePopover (report, brief and finished-head pills), .popover(arrowEdge: .bottom) plus presentedChrome (merge outcome, head steps, files, revert confirm), rightClickPopover (message menus) and AttachmentPreviewSlot panels anchored on NSViews that mount lazily after the first hover. A Windows port needs matching anchor-on-hover-then-click behaviour. Panels also close on onDisappear.

The move from fixed point sizes to text styles in B2 (.subheadline, .callout, .footnote, .caption2, .body) affects both files. The report's size table (11/12/10/10/13) comes from Apple's HIG, not from this repository, and the report says so. It rightly flags the chip xmark possibly growing from 9 to 10 pt. The same decision should be applied across every B2 bundle that made this change, so one pinned table is used port-wide.

Storage.attach (Storage.swift:162-172) also drops folders and failed imports silently, and it re-counts the cap when copies land. So the composer's notice counts only drops from the cap at call time, taken from `runtime.draft.attachments.count` before the asynchronous import. A porter should not expect the notice to report skipped folders.

The '/' path-separator and LF-only word-boundary assumptions (ComposerView.swift:446-449, 461, 1168, 1283) are Windows-specific risks. They likely recur in other bundles that use NSString lastPathComponent and ToolTitles.relativePath.
ByteCountFormatter(.file) strings (DownloadsPopover.swift:33-37) probably appear in other bundles too. The port needs one shared formatter with pinned outputs, not per-file guesses.

B2 AppZoom (UI/Common/AppZoom.swift, WindowManager.swift:175 `.modifier(AppZoomModifier(percent: model.settings.appZoom))`, key "appZoom" default 100, normalized to levels [75, 90, 100, 110, 125, 150, 175, 200]) is the only size control relevant to these swaps. Any R2 report that describes 1.6.2's `.system(size:)` -> text-style migration as enabling text scaling needs the same correction. The swaps keep the default sizes: .title2 17, .body 13, .callout 12, .subheadline 11, .footnote 10.

Popovers: whether `.popover` content and the AppKit NSPopover hosted by PromptEditorPopover inherit the window-root AppZoom scaleEffect is not shown by these files. The zoom is applied to the window content in WindowManager, not to popover windows. A zoom-parity check should cover the model chip popover and the follow-up editor.

`.opencodeGo` is a new B2 ProviderKind (Core/Models/Provider.swift:8, commit 0eeab427a "split OpenCode Zen and OpenCode Go"). EffortBrand.init's switch is exhaustive, so any other exhaustive per-provider switch in the port must add it too. The EffortBrand doc comment (EffortSlider.swift:851) still lists only "Codex, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode, Devin, Copilot, Command Code".

Deterministic hash noise: `value - value.rounded(.down)` (EffortSlider.swift:1345) and the positive-time `truncatingRemainder` calls need floor-based modulo in TypeScript. Other readers' Canvas and animation reports may carry the same `frac`/`mod` shorthand.
All six sha256 values in the report match the B2 files byte for byte, and lines_total (332, 66, 46, 692, 211, 479) are correct.

The B1->B2 description is complete and exact for all six files: every change is a fixed point size replaced by a text style of the same macOS default size (11 -> .subheadline, 12 -> .callout, 13 -> .body, 10 -> .footnote, 15 -> .title3, 17 -> .title2), a .secondary/.tertiary/Color.secondary.opacity(0.6) style replaced by Chrome.secondaryText, `trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)` replaced by `.trimmed`, or `nonisolated` added on DiffLinesView members. Two visible effects the porter should carry over: the DiffLineRow line numbers go from 60 percent secondary to full Chrome.secondaryText, and the DiffFileCard chevron and CommandPalette shortcut text go from .tertiary to Chrome.secondaryText, which is brighter in both themes unless Chrome.secondaryText is itself dimmer.

QuestionTab unresolved question 1 can be settled: DroppyCode/Core/Support/Text.swift:132 defines `var trimmed: String { trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) }`, so the B2 change to QuestionAnswers.collect does not change behaviour.

The fixed sizes left unchanged (QuestionTab indicator `.system(size: 14)`, DiffLinesView `.system(size: 11.5, design: .monospaced)`, WelcomeView "Droppy Code" `.system(size: 34, weight: .semibold)`, NoThreadView symbol `.system(size: 46, weight: .light)`) are correctly identified, so a text-size setting in the port must scale the text styles and leave these alone.

RootView WelcomeView renders the literal strings "Droppy Code" and "The coding app by Droppy. A calm, native home for your coding agents." (lines 310, 312). The report quotes them correctly. Whether they carry over verbatim is a PORT_CONTRACT branding decision, not a reader question.

Platform items a Windows port must replace, all present in the report: NSPopover .semitransient with local event monitors and keyCode 53 (DiffInspector), NSHostingView.fittingSize pre-measurement (QuestionTab), CGEventSource.secondsSinceLastEventType with kCGAnyInputEventType (RootView), NSPasteboard (CopyCommandButton), NSApp.applicationIconImage (WelcomeView), and Liquid Glass .glassEffect/.glass/.glassProminent in every file.

All four files moved from fixed point sizes to system text styles (.subheadline, .body, .callout, .footnote, .title3) between B1 and B2. The report correctly flags that the macOS point sizes behind them must be pinned from evidence. The exceptions still fixed in B2 are `.system(size: 12.5, weight: .medium)` (AboutUpdateViews.swift:220), `.system(size: 14, weight: .semibold)` (MCPKeyPanel.swift:127) and `.system(size: 10.5)` (MCPKeyPanel.swift:220), and the report records all three correctly.

Locale and platform formatting (Date .long, .relative(presentation: .named), ByteCountFormatStyle .file, percent with 0 fraction digits) appears in several places. The Windows port needs pinned output samples, not API names. The .file = decimal-units trap is the most likely to go wrong.

Several doc comments in these files describe behaviour that is absent (the head profiles in HydraPairEditor) or that lives elsewhere. Readers should mark comment-only claims apart from code-backed ones.

The HydraSettingsPage toggle detail at line 91 contains a literal em dash (U+2014): "on the same model — on a scale without a medium (Z.ai)". The report quotes it correctly. The port has to keep it verbatim for parity, whatever lint rule the port has on em dashes.

The `.trimmed` helper (Core/Support/Text.swift:132) is `.whitespacesAndNewlines`. Every B2 place that replaced `trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)` with `.trimmed` is behaviour-neutral. Readers of other bundles who list this as a B1->B2 change should say so.

Several reports describe view-lifecycle-bound behaviour (onChange on a card or page) as if it were global. In the port, the MCP setup-panel auto-open and the connect celebration and chime must stay tied to the MCP settings page and card being mounted to keep parity.

The B2 font change from fixed point sizes to SwiftUI text styles (.title, .title3, .body, .callout, .subheadline, .footnote, .caption2) runs across all three files. None of them states the point sizes, so the port needs one source-backed mapping table, not per-reader guesses.

Text in these files names macOS platform features: "this Mac" (MCPSettingsPage.swift:397, 637, 1043) and "Keychain" (lines 103, 814, 836, 880). The Windows wording must be decided in one place under the port contract.

NSCursor push/pop (ModelsSettingsPage.swift:120,139,189,192,198) relies on a cursor stack. Windows has none, so the balance rules (open hand on grip hover, closed hand during a drag, one pop at drag end, a leftover pop when released away from the grip) must be emulated explicitly.

The B2 typography sweep is not complete, and a porter should not normalise it. The new B2 provider header still uses fixed `.system(size: 13, weight: .semibold)` and chevron `.system(size: 11, weight: .semibold)` (SettingsView.swift:654,658). The provider card uses 13/11/12 monospaced (679,682,729,758), ThemePickerButton 12.5/8 (1199,1202) and the non-modifier keycap `.system(size: 14, weight: .semibold)` (ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:390).

Some strings contain non-ASCII characters the port must keep byte-exact: "Checking…" and "Checking providers…" and prompt "sk-…" use U+2026, "Native API · <host>" uses U+00B7, and the Composer chord "⌘ 1–9" uses U+2013 (en dash, not an em dash). The provider comments at SettingsView.swift:588,602 contain em dashes; they are source comments only, not UI text.

The Windows port needs Windows replacements for NSEvent local monitors, NSApplication.didResignActiveNotification, NSHapticFeedbackManager (no Windows equivalent), key code 53 (Escape), the ⌃⌥⇧⌘ glyphs, Keychain wording ("Stored in your Keychain"), revealInFinder, openTerminal and the Mac-only About and Credits copy ("for Mac", "built in Swift with Liquid Glass", SwiftTerm credit). The report's unresolved questions list these correctly.

Unverified here and left to other bundles: AppZoom.levels/normalized/next, whether chatZoom is migrated to appZoom, AppSettings.defaultBackdropOpacity, ShortcutStore.refusal texts, KeyChord.allowedModifiers, TokenActivityGrid.rows/monthTicks/tomorrow, TokenActivityMode titles and UsagePanel.tokens formatting. The report flags each honestly as unresolved.

The B2 change to this file is typography only: `.system(size: N)` became `.system(<TextStyle>)` in 5 places. This matches the pattern seen in DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/Popovers.swift and ProjectIconPicker.swift in the same diff. The port needs one shared mapping from text style to px (title, callout, subheadline, and so on), not a per-file guess.

Several view-level behaviours come from WallpaperStore (DroppyCode/UI/Theme/Wallpaper.swift): the didSet clamp and immediate persistence of "wallpaperSoftness", the "wallpaperFile" key, the live and full renders gated on fileURL, and the CIGaussianBlur rendering. Whoever reads Wallpaper.swift must cover them, and this card's port has to be wired to them.

Popover presentation depends on a row being realized and wrapped: `pendingDeletionID`, `pendingArchiveID` and `renaming` are plain ids or snapshots, and a popover appears only on a row that carries the matching wrapper and is currently built (a LazyVStack child, not collapsed). A Windows port that shows these dialogs globally (modal dialogs or a single overlay) would change upstream behavior for helpers, heads, collapsed projects and off-screen rows. The porter needs an explicit decision here.

Several one-shot model requests (archiveRequest, finishRequest, sidebarRevealThreadID) are consumed by the views in this file. finishRequest is consumed only by a SidebarThreadRow whose id matches and whose `reopens == isSettled` (1866-1870). If no such row is on screen, this file never consumes it. The fallback must be checked in AppModel, not assumed.

Every B1->B2 font change here moves from fixed points to text styles scaled by the new app-wide zoom (e6ec1f44d). The fixed sizes that remain (thread title 12/13 at lines 2042 and 2049, stub chevron 8 bold at line 1591) do NOT scale with that text-style zoom, so mixed scaling is upstream behavior and a Windows port should not normalize it.

All B1->B2 font changes in these files replace fixed sizes with text styles: 13->.body, 12->.callout, 11->.subheadline, 10->.footnote, 15->.title3. A Windows port needs one mapping table from text style to size (and any user text-size scaling) applied across UsageViews, UsagePanel, UsageFloatingPanel, TourView, TourWindowController and TerminalPanel. Fixed sizes remain on purpose: 28 bold for the tour title (TourView.swift:157, TourWindowController.swift:461), 40 for the photo placeholder (TourView.swift:271), and 12.5 medium for the floating 'Usage' title (UsageFloatingPanel.swift:86).

The terminal colours are duplicated. The panel background `Color(white: 0.08)` / `Color(white: 0.985)` (TerminalPanel.swift:107) must equal the terminal's `nativeBackgroundColor` `NSColor(white: 0.08, alpha: 1)` / `NSColor(white: 0.985, alpha: 1)` (TerminalStore.swift:188) so the drawer and the terminal blend. The port should keep them as one token.

TerminalFont's three sources (Ghostty, iTerm2, Terminal.app) do not exist on Windows. Without a decision on Windows sources (for example the Windows Terminal settings.json font face and size), the Windows result is always the no-configured-font path: `firstInstalledNerdFont(size: 12)` (the first installed family whose name contains "nerd font", case-insensitive) or the monospaced system font at 12. That is still defined behaviour and could be the parity target.

The tour's measured-height approach (TourWindowController.swift:416-436) depends on the text layout in the measuring view being identical to the rendered one. On Windows the measurement and the rendering must share fonts, padding and button chrome, or the fixed card clips or leaves slack.

The main window, Settings window and every capture window all use the one `let model = AppModel()` (line 13). A capture window therefore renders the user's live model state through `RootView()`, and its HostedRoot also writes NSApp.appearance on first appearance (lines 152-158, `initial: true`).

Four behaviours depend on AppKit semantics that the report leaves implicit, and each needs an explicit Windows decision: NSWindow.center() vertical bias (lines 43, 68, 82), y-up clamping (lines 51-52), `.rounded()` rounding rule (lines 48-49), and NSScreen.main meaning the key window's screen (line 50).

The port needs these related files, which the report lists as unresolved: AppZoomModifier (range and default of settings.appZoom), WindowChrome.configure, ThreadWindow's key chords for selectThread/selectThreadNumber, SecondaryWindow, DCDisplayCycleGuardedWindow, and AppTheme.spec.scheme/accent.

Swift synthesized Decodable ignores property default values: a non-optional `var x = default` is still a required key. This affects MCPConnection (isEnabled, values, tools), MCPCustomServer.Variable (isSecret), HydraHeadProfile (id, name) and HydraLanding.File (additions, deletions). Combined with the `container.value(_:default:)` helper (Coding.swift:5, `try?` over decodeIfPresent, so type mismatches also fall back), a single bad child element empties whole arrays: HydraPair.headProfiles and HydraLanding.files. A Windows port using zod/JSON defaults per field would be MORE tolerant than upstream; exact parity needs whole-array fallback semantics.

Swift String operations here work on grapheme clusters, not UTF-16: split(separator: "
") does not split CRLF, and count/prefix limits count graphemes (quoted 1_200/800, singleLine 60). A TS port must use a grapheme segmenter (Intl.Segmenter) and treat "
" as one unit to match. lineStartFences' `isNewline` check on the preceding Character treats "
" as a newline, which matches naive JS only by coincidence.

`.trimmed` (Text.swift:130-132, new in B2) is `trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)`: Unicode whitespace plus newlines, including U+0085, U+2028, U+00A0 and so on. JS String.prototype.trim covers a similar but not identical set (e.g. U+0085 NEL is trimmed by Foundation but not by JS trim). The B2 refactor changed no behavior, but the port needs a shared helper with Foundation's set.

Model-facing strings in Hydra.swift contain literal Mac/macOS wording ('any git repository on this Mac', MCPCustom 'Runs on this Mac:') and an em dash (Hydra.swift:745 Codex profile rule). The project's no-em-dash rule and exact-parity requirement conflict here and need an explicit decision under PORT_CONTRACT, not a silent substitution.

Several unresolved questions in the report are answerable from single files one hop away: JSONEncoder.storage (iso8601, sortedKeys), MCPProxy.url format (http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp/<id>), TextCleanup.singleLine truncation (limit-1 + "…"), AntiSlopPolicy.instructions(enabled:false) being non-empty, and HydraMergeRecord.label/url/project being optional. Readers should close these rather than defer them.

The report treats Swift property initial values as decode defaults in some places and not others. That rule matters for every persisted struct in this bundle: only fields decoded through `container.value(_:default:)` (TurnRecord and ThreadDocument) or declared Optional are tolerant. Every other non-optional field is required, and failing one drops the enclosing TimelineItem, FollowUpPrompt or HydraMergeRecord through Lenient (Coding.swift:11-17).

Unresolved questions should be checked against the cited helper before being left open. The report cites Hydra.swift line 1165 for withoutDelegationBlock but did not read the next three lines, which answer its own question.

Everything the report says is behaviour-neutral in B2 was verified against the diff. The B1->B2 changes to Shell.swift (OnceContinuation and OutputCollector moved from NSLock to Mutex), StdioProcess.swift (Mutex<State>) and the `.trimmed` adoption in JSONRPC/Shell change only locking and helper naming. All numbers, strings and timeouts are unchanged: 4,000/64,000/16,000 bytes, 3 s and 1 s kills, 120 s, 8 s and 3 s timeouts, -32000/-32601/-32603. The only B2 behaviour surface is the new ISO8601 enum and its adoption at HangWatchdog.swift:88.

The "parse or drop" choices a JS port would get wrong are scattered across files and would benefit from one shared helper spec. ISO8601.date(from:) is strict (bare dates rejected). StdioProcess.deliver strips only trailing 0x0D and 0x20 and silently drops unparseable lines. The JSONRPC handler treats a method with an unparseable id (such as null) as a notification and ignores a response with an unknown id.

Termination differs by path and should not be unified in the port without a decision. Shell.run escalates to SIGKILL after 1 s on the process group when the child leads it (`kill(getpgid(pid) == pid ? -pid : pid, SIGKILL)`). StdioProcess.terminate escalates after 3 s and signals only the pid (`kill(process.processIdentifier, SIGKILL)`), after closing stdin first.

The whitespace trim changes behaviour at no call site. B2 Text.swift:130-132 defines `var trimmed: String { trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) }`, and its doc says "narrower sets keep `trimmingCharacters(in:)`". That explains why Git.swift:712 still uses `.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)`. A port should map `trimmed` to one shared helper that trims whitespace AND newlines, and keep apply's conflict-path trim to spaces and tabs only.

ShellResult (Core/Support/Shell.swift l.9-19) decides several observable results here. `succeeded` is `status == 0`. output and errorOutput decode stdout and stderr as UTF-8. failureMessage is the trimmed stderr, else the trimmed stdout, else "The command failed with exit code \(status).". Every ShellError from Git.swift carries that text, so the port's process layer must reproduce it exactly.

Every git invocation on Windows depends on Git for Windows supporting `--pathspec-from-file`/`--pathspec-file-nul`, `rev-parse --path-format=absolute` and `cat-file -Z`. The report correctly leaves the minimum git version unresolved. The port needs its own probe or pinned git version, because presentPaths returns [] on any failure (l.347), which silently treats every path as untracked.

The ref namespace `refs/droppy-code/checkpoints/<uuid lowercased>/<turn>-<phase>` and the identity `Droppy Code <droppy-code@localhost>` are written into users' repositories. For a rebranded Windows port this needs a naming decision before the first release, because refs once written must stay readable.

Several behaviours in this bundle depend on Core/Support/JSONValue.swift, which the reader treated as out of scope and left unresolved, although it is short and answers the questions. .int accepts double and numeric string (lines 83-89). .bool accepts only a real JSON boolean (lines 99-102). parse uses JSONSerialization with .fragmentsAllowed (line 16). data() writes `.withoutEscapingSlashes`, with keys unsorted unless pretty (lines 59-62). JSON-RPC payloads in Hub and Probe therefore have unescaped slashes and unordered keys, while MCPOAuth's stored blobs (JSONSerialization `.sortedKeys` only) escape slashes.

Foundation URL semantics recur across files: URL.path strips trailing slashes and percent-decodes (MCPOAuth.swift:219, MCPProbe.swift:356); URLComponents query encoding leaves reserved characters raw (MCPOAuth.swift:581-598, 772-778); URLRequest timeoutInterval is an idle timeout (all four HTTP helpers). A Windows port on Node/Chromium URL and fetch semantics differs on each of these unless it emulates them deliberately.

Hub and Probe duplicate the JSON-RPC builders and initialize params (`protocolVersion "2025-06-18"`, clientInfo `{"name":"Droppy Code","version":"1.0"}`) but differ in session-id handling (Hub: initialize only; Probe: every response), reply matching (Hub buffers out-of-order replies; Probe discards non-matching lines), poll interval (10 ms vs 5 ms), and process tracking (Hub tracks; Probe does not). A shared Windows implementation must keep these differences.

Callers verified in B2: OpenAICompatibleSession.swift:510/898/904 (MCPHub tools/parse/call), MCPStore.swift:289 (reload), AppDelegate.swift:54 (terminateAll), MCPProxy.swift:334/347 (MCPOAuth.accessToken, called a second time on retry), MCPStore.swift:94/100/126/308-309/325/330 (signOut/isSignedIn/signIn). There is no caller of MCPOAuth.refreshIfNeeded. MCPProxy.swift changed materially between B1 and B2 (96 lines in the diff stat) and is not in this bundle, so the report's claim about how the Hub's HTTP entries get OAuth tokens via MCPProxy should be checked against that bundle's report.

The port lives in a mutable box read at resolve time (MCP.swift:165 `server.url = MCPProxy.url(for: id)`). Any Windows port must decide when to re-export provider configs after a re-pick. B2 never re-exports on its own, so the configs from the first launch can go stale for the rest of that session.
Only MCPStore.init (AppModel.swift:123 `mcp = MCPStore()`) starts the proxy, and nothing stops it. The proxy's lifetime is the app process.
In B2 every proxy route is OAuth-only with empty headers. Non-OAuth http servers bypass the proxy (MCP.swift:161-163 `.http(let url, let headers)` fills the url directly).
The B1->B2 changes to both files are refactors (a Mutex in place of NSLock; `.trimmed` in place of `trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)`). No behaviour delta needs porting.

All three B2 SHA-256 values in the report are of the CRLF working tree (the files have CRLF line endings), not of the git blobs. The B1 SHAs the report gives (564c13ed..., 54ef58c9...) match the CRLF working tree of E:/Droppy/reference/droppy-code. Anyone checking against `git show` output will get different hashes (for example the B2 ACPSession blob hashes to 1d969f4e...).

The only behaviour change from B1 to B2 in this bundle is in AntigravitySession: no `--allowed-mcp-server-names` argument, with MCP scoping moved to GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH (confirmed at ProviderRegistry.swift:277: `if provider == .antigravity, let path = MCPProviderConfig.geminiSettingsPath() { environment["GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH"] = path }`). The other change is fractional-second reset_time parsing through ISO8601.date(from:) (Core/Support/ISO8601.swift:19-21, fractional first, then plain). Every `.trimmed` replacement is equivalent to the old call, since Text.swift:132 defines `var trimmed: String { trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) }`.

Both sessions use the start-time configuration for launch flags (ACP launchArguments reads configuration.runtimeMode; Antigravity modeArguments reads configuration.*). ACP's per-turn runtimeMode affects only client-side auto-approval (automaticOption). The port must keep that split.

The ACPLaunchGate is one static instance on ACPSession (`private static let launchGate = ACPLaunchGate(spacing: 1.5)`). It is shared by all four ACP providers and by probeModels catalog probes, not kept per provider.

Turn-start asymmetry. Claude emits `.turnStarted(providerTurnID: nil)` synchronously in writeUserMessage, including for "/compact". Codex emits `.turnStarted(providerTurnID: id)` only from the turn/started notification. A shared Windows session layer must not synthesise .turnStarted at send time for Codex.

Failure-text asymmetry. A failed Claude turn always carries text (result, the joined errors, or "Claude stopped before finishing."). A failed Codex turn can carry error nil. Neither session emits .turnCompleted when the process dies mid-turn; each emits only .exited.

Spend identity differs by provider. Claude records `TokenLedger.shared.record(spend: spend.totalTokens)` without identity and emits TokenSpend with no agentID; head (task_progress) tokens are never recorded. Codex records by rollout id (lowercased in the ledger), and its head spend carries agentID and model from headModels. Neither .tokenSpend is wrapped in .agentEvent.

Both sessions put AntiSlopPolicy text into every launch (Claude `--append-system-prompt`, Codex `developerInstructions`), including the disabled 'off' notice. The port must send the off text, not omit it.

Neither static knownOptions (Claude) nor any Codex state is persisted by these files. The only persistence touched is TokenLedger's live state, saved by LiveSpendStateStore after a 2 s debounce (TokenLedger.swift:136-142, outside this bundle).

Windows: the mod's `import(bridgePath)` (CommandCodeAPI.swift:390) and PiCLI.swift:169's `await import(process.env.DROPPY_CODE_MCP_BRIDGE)` both pass a raw filesystem path to ESM import. On Windows both need file:// URL conversion, or MCP tools silently disappear, because the error is only console.error'd.

The approval grant buckets ("command"/"fileChange"/"tool", CommandCodeSession.swift:741-746) depend on ToolCall.kind values chosen in makeToolCall. Any porter that changes a tool's kind for display changes what 'Approve for session' covers.

Exit code 130 (CommandCodeSession.swift:445) and `process.ppid === 1` (CommandCodeAPI.swift:428) are both POSIX signals of process death. The report flags each, but on Windows the only reliable signals are interruptRequested and a separate parent-liveness check. The mod otherwise waits up to `6 * 60 * 60 * 1000` ms after Droppy dies.

The user-facing strings "Run `cmd login` in Terminal" and "Settings → Providers → Command Code" (CommandCodeSession.swift:470,506) are verbatim macOS wording, duplicated in two places (exit code 3 and friendlyError). A port must change both together.

The whitespace trimming changes in all four files are equivalent. Core/Support/Text.swift:132 is `var trimmed: String { trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) }`, and the report is right that they do not change behaviour.

DroppyCode/Core/Support/ISO8601.swift does not exist in B1 (dd2b86ef), so it is a new B2 dependency the port must provide before CopilotSession.parseDate. ISO8601.date tries `Date.ISO8601FormatStyle(includingFractionalSeconds: true)` and then `Date.ISO8601FormatStyle()`, and dateOnly is `.year().month().day()`. The report's claim that B2 now accepts fractional-second quota resetDate stamps is correct.

Grapheme versus code unit semantics recur. Swift String.count, prefix, split(separator:) and NSString ranges differ from JS string indexing. Any Windows port of NativeFileTools needs an explicit parity decision for CRLF and composed characters.

The Copilot permission flow has two approve-once shapes. Automatic approvals send `["kind": "approve-once"]` (line 811), and approvals the user clicks send `["kind": "approve-once", "approvedInteractively": true]` (line 277). The report records both, and the port must keep them separate.

Both files depend on ToolTitles.unwrapShell, and OpenAICompatibleSession also runs the unwrapped string as the command (line 1018). The Windows port must match unwrapShell exactly, because it changes what executes, not only the title.

OpenAICompatibleSession hard-codes /bin/zsh -lc (line 1157) and /usr/bin/grep (line 1136) with LoginEnvironment.current, and its system prompt says "on macOS." (line 1202). These are owner decisions for Windows and remain correctly UNRESOLVED in the report.

B2's ISO8601.string(from:) is `Date.ISO8601FormatStyle()` plain (whole seconds, UTC, Z), so the prompt date keeps the `2026-09-13T18:28:42Z` shape. Unlike the reader's unresolved question, this is settled from source for the format itself.

PiSession's unifiedDiff (lines 486-494) writes FileEdit.path as pi's raw (possibly absolute) path, while the row title uses ToolTitles.relativePath. Diff headers will read "--- a//abs/path" for absolute paths. On Windows, drive-letter paths would appear verbatim in headers.

The report's unresolved question about `.trimmed` is resolvable. B2 DroppyCode/Core/Support/Text.swift:132 defines `var trimmed: String { trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) }`, so all the `.trimmed` hunks in the six files are behaviour-neutral.

The ISO8601 helper (DroppyCode/Core/Support/ISO8601.swift) parses with `Date.ISO8601FormatStyle(includingFractionalSeconds: true)` and then `Date.ISO8601FormatStyle()`, not ISO8601DateFormatter. Because PlanLimits.parseDate strips `\.\d+` first, only the plain style ever matches. The port should parse `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` with a zone designator and should not rely on JS Date's looser parsing.

The API key is trimmed inconsistently across files. ZaiAPI.validate, listModels and planLimits trim. ZaiAPI.resetCredits receives the trimmed key. ProviderRegistry.consumeResetCredit, refreshAPIProvider and the refreshPlanLimits empty checks use the raw `settings.apiKey(for:)`. A port that normalises keys once changes observable status strings ('Not signed in' vs 'Not installed').

ProviderKind facts needed by R2-33 but outside it (B2 Provider.swift): `.opencodeGo` executableName is "opencode" (line 46), loginCommand is "opencode auth login" (68), iconName reuses "provider-opencode" (60), and usesACP includes .opencodeGo (104), so mergedACPCatalog applies to both halves.

Several reads touch credential material the port rules forbid reading: PlanLimits.swift:184-193 reads `.credentials.json` and the Keychain token, and ProviderRegistry.swift:853 reads `~/.grok/auth.json`. The report flags both as unresolved. A contract decision is required before porting.

TokenActivitySection.swift:93-98 drives both grid recomputation (`.onChange(of: GridKey(daily: ledger.dailyTotals, mode: mode), initial: true)`) and the scan trigger (`.task`). The R-report for TokenActivitySection should be checked against this file's claim that the scan is 'one-time background'. Per process it runs once, but it is lazy: it runs on the first Settings General visit.

B2 eventDate now delegates to DroppyCode/Core/Support/ISO8601.swift:19-21: `(try? fractional.parse(text)) ?? (try? plain.parse(text))`, with `fractional = Date.ISO8601FormatStyle(includingFractionalSeconds: true)` and `plain = Date.ISO8601FormatStyle()`. B1 used ISO8601DateFormatter with [.withInternetDateTime, .withFractionalSeconds], then [.withInternetDateTime]. The report rightly leaves open whether offsets other than Z and fractional parts longer than 3 digits parse the same way. The Windows port should pin its accepted shapes to whatever the ISO8601.swift reader establishes, not to B1.

Storage.root (Storage.swift:19-25) is `CaptureRun.storageRoot` when set, otherwise Application Support/<AppInfo.name>. The report says only 'Application Support'. That is correct for normal runs, but capture runs move all three token-activity JSON files too. The legacy fingerprint key always uses UserDefaults.standard (line 305/308), even in a capture run, while liveDaily uses `CaptureRun.defaults ?? .standard`. The report states this split correctly.

AppDelegate.swift:52 `TokenLedger.shared.flushLiveSpend()` in applicationWillTerminate will create the singleton at quit if nothing touched it earlier, which loads token-activity-live-v2.json and rolls liveCodex into settledCodex in memory only. No save follows, because liveSave is nil. This is harmless, but a port with eager construction behaves the same way.

B2's switch from fixed sizes to text styles is exactly size-preserving on macOS (callout 12, subheadline 11, body 13, title3 15, title2 17, footnote 10 replace 12/11/13/15/17/10). The report records every hunk correctly. The open decision it raises is real: does the Windows port honour system text scaling? No source can answer it.

Accessible names come from three mechanisms: Text(help) on the icon and text buttons, Text(verbatim: title) on segments and tiles, and nothing on ChromeTextMenu, GlassPickerButton and RowActionsButton. The report records them only in part. A port should carry an explicit accessible-name table per control.

Two popover close paths exist: closePopoverBox for AppKit-hosted NSPopover and dismiss() for SwiftUI popovers. Action ordering differs by path: deferred Task in the plain case, synchronous in the confirmation case and in the context menu. On Windows, where menus will probably be custom flyouts, this ordering matters for actions that open dialogs.

Verified exact: the 131-entry emoji list (including the FE0F variation selectors and the ZWJ sequence U+1F9D1 U+200D U+1F3EB) and the 56-entry symbol shortlist in the report match the source codepoint for codepoint.

The deleted B1 file DroppyCode/UI/Common/ChatZoom.swift (71 lines) is the counterpart to both AppZoom.swift and ChatFont.swift, and this bundle's report never mentions it. Check that some bundle records the deletion, the dropped "chatZoom" UserDefaults key, and the removal of the Settings > General chat text-size slider with its sample chat (B1 ChatZoom.swift:4-5). Any port work already done from B1 for chat zoom has to be removed or replaced.

The macOS text-style point sizes (B1 ChatZoom.swift:45-56) are the only exact size table found in upstream. Every Windows file that ports `.caption`, `.callout`, `.body` or `.headline` should use it rather than guessing.

Several UI strings are macOS-specific but must be kept verbatim for parity ("Show in Finder" at AttachmentPreview.swift:360). The port contract has to decide whether the Windows build keeps the literal string or maps it; the report does not raise this.

B2 removed `@Environment(\.chatZoom)` from InlineText, ProseRunView, MarkdownBlockView and CodeBlock. InlineText now computes `let scaled = (pointSize * 2).rounded() / 2` (was `pointSize * zoom * 2`), and mentionText uses `let size: CGFloat = 16` (was `16 * zoom`). The pointSize fed into LinkParagraphView is no longer zoom-scaled in B2. That changed behaviour sits in the caller, not in this bundle.

B2 FaviconCache.iconData (MarkdownView.swift) now fetches only `https://\(host)/favicon.ico` with `request.timeoutInterval = 5`. It no longer uses `icons.duckduckgo.com/ip3` or the `google.com/s2/favicons` fallback. This decides whether `FaviconCache.cached(host:)` gives LinkParagraphView a 14x14 favicon attachment at all.

The dimmed-colour change is made the same way in three places: LinkParagraphView.swift:121, ProseRunView.swift (`let color = dimmed ? NSColor.labelColor.withAlphaComponent(0.7) : NSColor.labelColor`) and StreamVeil.swift VeiledText (`dimmed ? Color.primary.opacity(0.7) : Color.primary`). Quote blocks and CodeBlock/TableBlock captions moved from `.secondary` to `Chrome.secondaryText`. A port should change all of these together.

The hover callers MarkdownView.swift:1165-1192 and ProseRunView.swift:31-58 call HydraHeadHoverPopover.show only when `targets[name]` exists, `target.url == url` and `personasByName[name]` exists, and only when the hovered threadID changes. They call hide() on `.ended` and in onDisappear. The pointing hand comes from `NSCursor.pointingHand.push()/pop()` driven by `view.hasLink(at:)`, not from the `.cursor` in linkTextAttributes, which has no effect because resetCursorRects is empty.

`Coordinator.lastHeads` is dead in LinkParagraphView, but the parallel ProseRunView coordinator does use `lastHeads` (ProseRunView.swift:99,105) in its rebuild check. A porter merging the two representables should keep that difference.

Cache keys follow the text actually passed to RichLink. Any caller that passes a composite string (ProseRunView's joinedSources) both pollutes prettyCache and fails to invalidate what is rendered. A Windows port should key pretty/asset invalidation per paragraph source, or reproduce the stale-title behaviour on purpose.

Two render paths with different visuals exist for the same markdown. SwiftUI per-block (streaming only in B2): accent-coloured circle markers, SF Symbol checkboxes, quote bar, Font.chat text-style headings, headings with links at 13 pt. AppKit ProseRunView (all finished messages): text glyph markers in label colour, no quote bar, multiplier headings forced semibold. When a stream finishes, the message visibly switches from the first to the second. A parity port must implement both and switch at the same moment.

B2 favicon fetching contacts every public linked host directly (`https://<host>/favicon.ico`, 5 s timeout, URLSession.shared) as soon as a message renders. A timeout or error puts the host into `failed` for the rest of the process with no retry. This is a network and privacy behaviour the port must copy exactly, and in-code comments at MarkdownView.swift:918-919 and 1056-1058 still describe the old third-party service.

The report leaves as unresolved whether `Color.primary.opacity(0.7)` (StreamVeil.swift:311) matches the dimmed colour used elsewhere. The B1->B2 diff answers it: it is one coordinated change. LinkParagraphView.swift:121 went from `let textColor = dimmed ? NSColor.secondaryLabelColor : NSColor.labelColor` to `dimmed ? NSColor.labelColor.withAlphaComponent(0.7) : NSColor.labelColor`. ProseRunView.swift:161 made the same change from `NSColor.secondaryLabelColor`. Several MarkdownView.swift sites went from `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` to `.foregroundStyle(Chrome.secondaryText)`. The Windows port should define one 'dimmed = primary text at 0.7' token and use it on every path.

Citations verified at B2: MarkdownView.swift:84 and :100 (`.environment(\.markdownVeiled, isStreaming)`), :317 (`VeiledText(segments: segments)`), :871 (`var markdownDimmed: Bool`), :1203, :1300; LinkParagraphView.swift:42 (`let veiled = context.environment.markdownVeiled`), :57 (`view.streamVeil.update(view, active: veiled)`), :76 (`view.streamVeil.detach(view)`), :290 (`let streamVeil = LinkTextVeil()`); RenderBudget.swift:13 (`final class ScrollActivity`, `isScrolling` at :16); Chrome.swift:87 (`static var accentNSColor: NSColor { ThemeManager.spec.accent.map { NSColor($0) } ?? .controlAccentColor }`). The report omits LinkParagraphView.swift:57 and :76, the update and detach call sites that drive LinkTextVeil.

B1->B2: the report correctly lists three hunks (@@ -297,8 +297,8, @@ -308,7 +308,7, @@ -324,10 +324,10) and correctly says the 431-line length is unchanged. The `out + t` to `Text("\(out)\(t)")` change has no visible effect on Windows; only the Color.secondary to Color.primary.opacity(0.7) change affects rendering.

ThemeManager.current is written from two places, AppSettings.theme's didSet (AppSettings.swift:289) and AppSettings init (AppSettings.swift:728). The reports for AppSettings.swift and for the picker in SettingsView.swift (lines 1180-1231) should agree with this file on the persistence key "appTheme", the legacy "appearance" fallback and the System, Dark, Light section order.

didChange listeners are HydraButton.swift:479 and WorkingIndicators.swift:185. WorkingIndicators also reads ThemeManager.current directly (lines 78, 107, 259), so their reports should record that they take the AppTheme itself, not only the ThemeSpec.

The Keychain service name and the data folder are set by Info.plist values defined in these build files: CFBundleDisplayName becomes the kSecAttrService, and the exact bundle id 'iordv.droppycode.dev' selects '.droppy-code-dev' over '.droppy-code'. The readers of APIKeychain.swift, MCPKeychain.swift, Text.swift and Storage.swift must carry these exact values into the Windows secret store and data folder names. The Dev variant must also keep its separate secret namespace ('Droppy Code Dev') and folder, and keep updates and legacy migration switched off.

The release notes reach two surfaces through two different transformations. The GitLab release and in-app About path uses build_changelog.py --section: `###` becomes `##`, emphasis is NOT stripped, the Thanks block is included but skipped by AboutUpdateViews.swift, and file order is kept. The website path uses build_releases: strip_emphasis deletes every '_' and '*', and SECTION_ORDER forces New features / Bug fixes / Refinements. A Windows About view has to parse the `## ` form, and exact-parity text should come from the CHANGELOG, not from changelog.json.

The B2 build is labelled 1.6.2 build 20, but the CHANGELOG's Unreleased block (lines 9-18) says four more areas have already merged into the B2 source: the Hydra token and timing panel, the restored design with the judgment service removed, native providers running up to four concurrent automatic read tools, and the token-activity measured/inherited split. The readers of those Swift files must confirm them, because nothing in these four files defines them.

The standard macOS About panel is still reachable: AppCommands.swift replaces .appSettings, .saveItem, .newItem and .help but not .appInfo. The B2 NSHumanReadableCopyright string "Copyright © 2026 Jordy Spruit (Droppy). Droppy Code by Jordy Spruit (Droppy), https://getdroppycode.app. GNU AGPL v3.0 with additional attribution terms." is therefore user-visible, and a Windows port needs an equivalent surface. Settings' LicensesRow (SettingsView.swift:1032-1042, detail "AGPL-3.0 with attribution terms, and the notices for what the app builds on.") reads the LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES and TRADEMARK resources that project.yml:30-35 bundles.
thin_reports: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Hydra.swift - thin only for the prompt texts. Structure, constants, roster, decode defaults, merge messages and the B1->B2 delta are covered well. But the largest model-facing strings are paraphrased or only partly quoted: policy() body :766-789, fallbackPolicy() body :960-968, workerPrompt/scoutPrompt :793-804, howToWork bullets 2-4 :676-678, the per-provider howToSpawn/howToWait :754-764, and the reportMessage closing sentences :1337-1384. Exact-parity prompts cannot be built from the report; they must be copied byte for byte from source, including the nine-space run at :961, the trailing newline from :788 and the double space when howToSpawn is empty.

DroppyCode/Services/Providers/CopilotSession.swift - The purpose and RPC coverage are good. The session.event mapper cannot be ported from this record alone, for three reasons. It gives almost no data keys per event (toolCallId, toolName, mcpServerName, messageId, deltaContent, reasoningId, requestId, permissionRequest, promptRequest, partialOutput, progressMessage and others are missing). It omits four handled events (permission.completed, session.warning, tool.execution_partial_result, tool.execution_progress). And its tool and permission tables give fallbacks without the primary fields, the ToolCall/ApprovalRequest kinds or the FileEdit construction.

DroppyCode.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj - the build settings are recorded carefully, but persisted_fields gets the runtime meaning wrong: it credits the bundle id with Keychain scoping and does not list CFBundleDisplayName as the Keychain service key. It also leaves out the Dev-variant behaviour that hangs on the bundle id string. A porter cannot choose the correct Windows secret-store or data-folder names from this record alone.

project.yml - accurate for its 59 lines, but calls_into misses scripts/release.sh:19 and scripts/release_credits.py:25,37 as readers of MARKETING_VERSION, and never says the double quotes on lines 13-14 are required by their regexes.
